events.subject: Sri Sita Devi
events.name: Sita Navami
events.short_description: Appearance day festival for Sri Sita Devi. The calendar matches it by the configured tithi rule.
events.full_description:
Srimati Sita Devi is the daughter of King Janaka and the consort of Lord Ramachandra. She is Lakshmiji herself, the eternal consort of Lord Narayana and the goddess of fortune. Her adoptive father found little Sita in the forest and immediately saw how much she resembled Lakshmi Devi. In time, however, he forgot this and loved her simply as his own daughter.

Once Sita Devi was walking in the forest with her friends. The girls tried in every way to reach a high branch, but they could not. Sita then went to the palace and quietly entered the room where the famous bow of Lord Shiva was kept, the bow with which he had fought Lord Vishnu. It normally took three thousand men to move the chariot on which that bow rested. Yet "little" Sita easily lifted the bow and quietly left the room. A guard standing nearby could hardly believe his eyes and immediately ran to the king. Sitaji shot down the branch and calmly returned the bow to its place. The ministers who gathered because of this extraordinary event told Janaka, "O king, Maha-Lakshmi lives in your house. All the signs show this clearly. How will you arrange Her marriage? If She is Lakshmiji, then you must find Sri Narayana, Her eternal Lord." Thus, later, Lord Ramachandra, Narayana Himself, came to the contest arranged by the father of Srimati Sita Devi and strung that bow. Such is the wondrous lila of the union of the eternal Divine Couple, Lord Narayana and Lakshmi Devi.

Just before His coronation, in obedience to the will of His father, Ramachandra went into exile for fourteen years together with Sita Devi and Lakshman. They lived in the forest, and there the lila took place in which Sita Devi was abducted by the wicked demon Ravana and held captive in Lanka. Searching for Sita, Rama besieged Lanka and killed Ravana. Yet before Rama accepted her back, Sita, to prove her fidelity to her Lord, had to pass through the trial of fire. Everyone stood still as Sita entered the blazing flames, but the tongues of fire could not harm Rama's faithful wife. In this way Sita proved her purity in thought, word, and deed.

After returning to Ayodhya, Rama learned that His subjects still suspected Sita of unfaithfulness and sent her to the forest. There she found shelter with the saintly sage Valmiki Muni, who raised her and Rama's two sons, Lava and Kusha. When the sons of Sita and Rama had grown, Valmiki returned her to Rama. But upon meeting Ramachandra, Sita asked her mother, the Earth, to receive her.

events.subject: Lord Balarama
events.name: Sri Balarama Purnima
events.short_description: Appearance day festival for Lord Balarama. The calendar matches it by the configured tithi rule.
events.full_description:
O Keshava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who has assumed the form of Lord Balarama and holds a plow in Your hands! All glories to You! Upon Your brilliant white body are garments the color of a fresh blue raincloud. These garments have the same color as the beautiful dark hue of the Yamuna River, who becomes greatly afraid when You strike her with Your plow.

Sri Baladeva is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. He also possesses the supreme authority of the Supreme Lord, and yet whenever Krishna appears, Sri Baladeva appears as Krishna's brother, sometimes as His elder brother and sometimes as His younger brother. In His vaibhava-prakasha form, the Lord manifests Himself as Balarama. Balarama looks just like Krishna; the only difference is that Krishna's bodily color is dark, while Balarama's is fair. These two Lords, Krishna and Balarama, are the seed and source of the universe, the Creator and Master of His creative energy. They enter the hearts of all living beings. They are the original Supreme Lords.

Sri Baladeva is the seventh child of Devaki. He is older than Krishna and has a white complexion. The following story is connected with this. The devas received instruction from Mahavishnu to take birth as gopalas, cowherd boys. Then Mahavishnu took one white hair from His head and said that it would be placed in the womb of Rohini and become Balarama; taking a black hair, He said that it would be placed in the womb of Yashoda and become Krishna. It is said that the white color signifies enlightenment.

Yogamaya transferred Ananta Shesha, Balarama, from the womb of Devaki to the womb of Rohini. After seven months, at the most auspicious moment in the month of Shravana, Rohini gave birth to Lord Balarama in complete happiness. His complexion was like a white lotus, and He looked like the full moon. His eyes shone like two bright rays of light, and His hair was the color of a fresh cloud, shining like the sun. He possessed such extraordinary beauty because He was none other than Lord Sankarshana. The astrologers predicted that He would have long arms and would kill Pralambasura, and that He would have a younger brother who would kill many other demons. They said that He was Dhenupal, protector of the cows and killer of Dhenukasura.

At Vasudeva's instruction, the brahmanas performed the jata-karma samskara ceremony. Although He was extraordinarily beautiful, everyone was very anxious because He was silent and motionless. No one could make Him utter a sound or move. Once, when Devaki was pregnant, she picked Him up and gently placed Him on her lap, near her heart where Krishna was present. Balarama immediately began to laugh and play like a carefree child. But when Devaki put Him down from her lap, He again became motionless. He remained in this state until His younger brother Krishna appeared. Lord Balarama had six brothers through His mother Rohini: Gada, Sarana, Durdhana, Vipula, Dhruva, and Krita.

Bala in Sanskrit means "strength." Lord Balarama embodies the strength by which one can approach Krishna. This is not physical strength, nor the strength of the mind. It is said that one cannot reach the spiritual world even by moving at the speed of thought. What material strength, then, could help us reach it? The spiritual strength given by Lord Balarama is the desire to serve God and the taste for that service. In essence, it is spiritual joy, Rama. The joy of spiritual life is found in service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Lord Balarama shows this by His own example. The shastras say that Balarama differs from Krishna only in bodily color. Krishna is the color of a raincloud, Shyama, while Balarama is the color of crystal. In all other respects They are equal. Yet Balarama voluntarily accepts a subordinate position.

Krishnadas Kaviraj Goswami writes that Balarama serves Krishna in three moods: as elder brother, as friend, and as servant. He does everything to please Krishna exactly as Krishna desires at each moment. This is the ideal servant of God: he accepts the position in which the Lord wants to see him. Balarama teaches us the same lesson. We should serve Krishna without attachment to any particular position, whether in the spiritual world or the material world, in heaven or in hell, as senior or junior. Lord Balarama is the original Guru.

events.subject: Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
events.name: Sri Gaura Purnima
events.short_description: Appearance day festival for Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. The calendar matches it by the configured tithi rule.
events.full_description:
There was no limit to the joy in the house of Sri Jagannath Mishra. Joy reigned in the room of Sri Shachidevi. With the appearance of the full and spotless moon on that day, the whole world was flooded by the current of Harinama. The moon in the sky hid its face in humility. How could it do otherwise? The moons upon His toes radiated such brilliant and auspicious light that they eclipsed millions of moons, for on this day Gaurachandra appeared. Flowers rained everywhere from the sky. Millions of conches and drums sounded, and celestial beings began to dance. The whole earth cried, "Jaya! Jaya!" and the entire universe attained liberation. Thus the news of Gaura Hari's appearance spread everywhere. All the devotees immediately felt deep fulfillment. The sweet sounds of conches, bells, mridangas, and karatals became still more beautiful when joined by the chorus of voices chanting, "Jaya Shachinandana! Jaya Gaura Hari!"

That night all the devotees came to the sacred Ganga to bathe and chant the Holy Names of the Lord together. Sri Advaita Acharya, who was then in Shantipur, suddenly began to dance. He seized Haridas, and together they loudly sang and danced. Extraordinary happiness filled the air; everyone could feel it.

Several brahmanas came to the house of Jagannath Mishra. They were overjoyed to see the infant radiating light like molten gold and immediately blessed the child. The wives of Lord Brahma, Shiva, Nrisimhadeva, Indra, and other devas also visited the house. Disguised as brahmana ladies, they brought various gifts for the Lord. Jagannath Mishra and Shachi Devi were deeply happy: a child who would deliver all three worlds had been born in their home.

Overwhelmed with joy at the birth of his dear son, Sri Jagannath Mishra held a splendid festival on the following day.

Sita Thakurani, the wife of Advaita Acharya, gave the Lord the name Nimai. He had been born beneath a neem tree, and neem is said to protect against witches and sorcerers; evil spirits also cannot remain near it. Thus Sita Thakurani named the Lord Nimai so that nothing could harm Him. Others called Him Gaurahari, the Golden Lord, because He looked like molten gold.

Once, while little Nimai was lying in His cradle, His parents saw various marks upon His feet: a flag, club, conch, and fish. Such marks can appear only upon the body of an avatar, an incarnation of the Lord. His parents continually saw these astonishing footprints upon the floor and could not understand where they came from.

While His parents discussed this, Nimai began to cry. Mother Shachi quickly took Him into her arms and lovingly breastfed Him. Jagannath Mishra decided to ask the astrologer Nilambar Chakravarti about the marks on his son's feet. He invited him to come and explain their meaning. Nilambar Chakravarti smiled affectionately and said, "This child's body bears all the signs of a great soul. His palms and the soles of His feet display the marks of Lord Narayana. This child can deliver all three worlds."

Fortunate souls can see Lord Chaitanya. Everything connected with Gaura Hari is eternal: His name, form, pastimes, associates, attributes, and all else. His appearance is eternal. The eternal Lord dwells within the souls of those fortunate people whose hearts are pure. Such truths cannot be grasped by our feeble reason. The Lord is achintya-bhedabheda, inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference, appearing in the form of Acharyadeva as the highest manifestation of this principle. By the mercy of sadhu and Guru, we may understand the glory of Sri Chaitanyadeva, the eternally pure, fully liberated Supreme Reality. Those fortunate souls who receive the mercy of the sadhu can understand that Gaurachandra appeared as Sri Krishna in the mood of Radharani. They feel great ecstasy in their hearts and can understand: "Gaurachandra performs His divine lilas even today, but only a few fortunate souls can see them."

Radiating the brilliance of molten gold, He appeared in the age of Kali to distribute by His causeless mercy what no previous avatar had given: the most elevated and radiant spiritual mellows of devotion to Himself.

events.subject: Lord Krishna
events.name: Sri Krishna Janmashtami
events.short_description: Appearance day festival for Lord Krishna. The calendar matches it by the configured tithi rule.
events.full_description:
Whenever religion declines on earth and irreligion prevails, I descend Myself, O descendant of Bharata. To deliver the righteous and punish the wicked, I appear on earth age after age. (Lord Krishna to Arjuna, Bhagavad-gita, Chapter 4, verses 7-8)

When the time came for Lord Krishna's appearance, all the constellations took the most auspicious positions. At that moment an atmosphere of peace and prosperity spread everywhere, in the east, west, south, and north. Auspicious combinations of stars were visible in the sky, and on earth, in all towns and villages, on the pasturing grounds, and in the minds of people, happiness prevailed. (Krishna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Chapter 3)

Sri Krishna Janmashtami is the appearance day of Lord Krishna. Lord Krishna appeared on our planet, but one should not think that He was born in the same way we are born. There are 8,400,000 species of life, and as long as we exist in the material world we take birth again and again, moving from one species to another. Krishna's birth is different. Therefore Krishna says that His birth should not be understood as ordinary, but as a special appearance. One who understands this is immediately liberated from the material world. How can one realize this truth? The Bhagavad-gita explains it.

One who wishes to know God, Krishna, truly and not superficially, takes to the path of devotional service, bhakti. Bhakti, devotional service to Krishna, is wonderful. Celebrating Janmashtami is also bhakti. Janmashtami is celebrated by all Hindus, whether they are Vaishnavas or not. The festival is observed in every home, just as Christmas is celebrated in Western countries.

Why does God come to earth? To reveal to the whole world His sweet pastimes. Every birth is a mystery. How much more mysterious, then, is the birth of the Unborn? The appearance of the Unmanifest. The Lord is everywhere, but who can recognize Him between atoms or photons of light? Therefore the Lord says that if a person simply understands this mystery, liberation will not delay.

Our contact with the world takes place through the senses. The eyes interact with streams of light in which various forms are seen; the ears absorb sounds; the nostrils relate to fragrances. By analyzing all forms of interaction between the senses and their objects, we come to understand that they in turn are objects observed by our inner self. Then, if through yoga we are able to perceive our own mind, we understand that our self has nothing to do with the mind either. Thus we come to understand ourselves as the observer. We observe this world through our eyes, ears, tongue, and so on, like a researcher of the ocean depths descending in a bathyscaphe. Reflecting on the nature of the observer and the observed, we may conclude that the observer is conscious and alive, while the observed does not possess consciousness. And yet the whole world seems alive to us. This means that behind this world stands the Supreme Observer, the Supreme Self, the Supersoul. In this way we become convinced of the existence of God.

The entire material creation is nothing but a veil through which the soul is able not to see, not to hear, and not to touch the Lord. Therefore, to show mercy to the souls living here, the Lord from time to time manifests Himself. His form belongs by nature to an entirely different category. While we look at the world through material senses, the Lord sees all universes, including our planet, and He does so not by means of limited material instruments, but through His own personal senses, which have a completely different, spiritual nature.

All the activities of the Lord and of the eternally liberated souls, His servants, are spiritual. His birth here is the manifestation of His eternal internal energy, and all the Lord's devotees are also under the protection of this energy, which allows the soul to enter its original state of eternity, knowledge, and bliss. Krishna's birth is a unique event. It is a festival of the soul, eternally free, loving, and happy. Although on earth it is celebrated once a year, this day can draw the soul into Eternity, where there is no suffering, no birth and death, but eternal life and the great adventure of love; where all dreams are fulfilled, where real life is vibrant, where souls laugh and weep from happiness, and where the soul finds itself.

events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Нитьянанда Трайодаши - день явления Господа Нитьянанды (пост)". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
The great saint Vrindavan Das Thakur says that this festival is filled with unlimited mercy. Sri Nityananda came as the principal associate of Lord Chaitanya. By serving Gauranga with complete self-giving, He teaches us what can make us truly happy. This is expressed in His very name: "eternal bliss." By worshiping Lord Nityananda, one attains love and devotion to the lotus feet of Krishna.

Nityananda was born in 1474 in the village of Ekachakra in Radhadesh. As a child, He constantly played with His friends, imitating the pastimes of Krishna, and in this way He spent the first twelve years of His life. On the day in 1486 when Sri Chaitanya was born in Navadvipa, Nityananda cried out in joy. After that, by divine arrangement, Nitai set out on pilgrimage to various holy places throughout North and South India in order to purify them from the sins left there by pilgrims. He remained engaged in this way until His twentieth year. On the path He seemingly met Madhavendra Puri by chance and accepted him as His Guru. For many days Nityananda traveled in the company of Madhavendra Puri, discussing Krishna's pastimes with him.

While Lord Gaurachandra was growing up in Navadvipa, Nityananda remained in Vrindavan. Sri Nityananda thought to Himself, "Chaitanya lives in Navadvipa, but His divine glory remains hidden. As soon as He decides to reveal His divinity, I will immediately go to Navadvipa and fulfill my role in serving Him." Only in 1506 did Lord Nityananda set foot on the blessed land of Nadia. The joy of the meeting between Lord Vishvambhar and Lord Nityananda cannot be expressed in words; tears of joy flowed constantly from Their eyes.

After Lord Chaitanya accepted sannyasa and settled in Jagannath Puri, absorbed in meditation on Krishna's pastimes, He asked Lord Nityananda to preach in Bengal on His behalf. There Nityananda manifested Himself as the savior of the most fallen. He gave Lord Chaitanya's mercy even to the most hardened wrongdoers. For Nityananda there is no one "unworthy of mercy". He bestows it upon everyone; one need only begin to serve Him. Bhaktivinod Thakur describes a good way to serve Him:

"In the town of Nadia, on the island of Godrum, Lord Nityananda opened the marketplace of the Holy Name for the deliverance of all fallen souls. O people, believe this! By the order of Lord Gauranga I have come to beg you, O brothers: chant the name of Krishna, worship Krishna, and give Krishna to others!"

The year of Nityananda Prabhu's disappearance is not known with certainty; according to one tradition, it was 1541.

Nityananda Prabhu is non-different from Krishna and possesses all six opulences. The only difference is Their bodies and moods. Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the original Guru of the universe, whose very principle of life is service to the Lord.

In the role of servant, Nityananda expands Himself to become the Lord's shoes, His garments, His seat, His bed, the Dham, and His abode. In the material world Sri Nityananda Prabhu expands Himself as Maha Vishnu, Garbhodakashayi Vishnu, and Kshirodakashayi Vishnu; He creates and maintains the entire cosmic manifestation.

In the role of teacher, Lord Nityananda comes into the material world to show by His own example how to serve the Lord with pure devotion. All true spiritual teachers are representatives, manifestations of the mercy of Nityananda Prabhu. He fulfills the desire of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu: to give Krishna consciousness even to the most fallen and unqualified.

Why does God come to earth? To reveal to the whole world His sweet pastimes. Every birth is a mystery. How much more mysterious, then, is the birth of the Unborn? The appearance of the Unmanifest. The Lord is everywhere, but who can recognize Him between atoms or photons of light? Therefore the Lord says that if a person simply understands this mystery, liberation will not delay.

Our contact with the world takes place through the senses. The eyes interact with streams of light in which various forms are seen; the ears absorb sounds; the nostrils relate to fragrances. By analyzing all forms of interaction between the senses and their objects, we come to understand that they in turn are objects observed by our inner self. Then, if through yoga we are able to perceive our own mind, we understand that our self has nothing to do with the mind either. Thus we come to understand ourselves as the observer. We observe this world through our eyes, ears, tongue, and so on, like a researcher of the ocean depths descending in a bathyscaphe. Reflecting on the nature of the observer and the observed, we may conclude that the observer is conscious and alive, while the observed does not possess consciousness. And yet the whole world seems alive to us. This means that behind this world stands the Supreme Observer, the Supreme Self, the Supersoul. In this way we become convinced of the existence of God.

The entire material creation is nothing but a veil through which the soul is able not to see, not to hear, and not to touch the Lord. Therefore, to show mercy to the souls living here, the Lord from time to time manifests Himself. His form belongs by nature to an entirely different category. While we look at the world through material senses, the Lord sees all universes, including our planet, and He does so not by means of limited material instruments, but through His own personal senses, which have a completely different, spiritual nature.

All the activities of the Lord and of the eternally liberated souls, His servants, are spiritual. His birth here is the manifestation of His eternal internal energy, and all the Lord's devotees are also under the protection of this energy, which allows the soul to enter its original state of eternity, knowledge, and bliss. Krishna's birth is a unique event. It is a festival of the soul, eternally free, loving, and happy. Although on earth it is celebrated once a year, this day can draw the soul into Eternity, where there is no suffering, no birth and death, but eternal life and the great adventure of love; where all dreams are fulfilled, where real life is vibrant, where souls laugh and weep from happiness, and where the soul finds itself.

After killing a demon who had assumed the form of a bull, Krishna, exhilarated by His victory, came to meet Radhika. Seeing Krishna stained with the bull's blood, Radha forbade Him to approach Her. Krishna tried to explain that it had been a shape-shifting demon and that He was very happy and proud to have defeated it. But Radha remained firm. She reminded Krishna that the bull represents religion, and that killing a bull, like killing a cow, is a very grave sin. Radha said that until Krishna purified Himself of the sin of killing a bull, She would not meet with Him.

"What should I do?" Krishna pleaded. "You must bathe in all the holy tirthas," Radha replied. Krishna then mystically created a large hollow and called all the sacred waters of the universe to come there. The presiding deities of all the holy rivers and lakes appeared before Krishna and filled the lake with their waters. It became known as Shyama Kunda. After bathing in that lake, Krishna appeared before Radharani. But noticing that some pride in His victory still remained in Krishna's heart, Radha told Him, "It seems the consequences of Your sin are very heavy; even all the sacred tirthas of the universe could not purify You."

Then Radha and Her friends removed their bracelets and began digging another hollow beside Shyama Kunda with them. They worked for many hours. When it was ready, Radha stood at its edge, raised Her arms, and prema flowed from Her heart into the hollow, soon filling it to the brim. Deeply moved, Krishna entered the water of this lake and emerged transformed to meet Radha. "Now You are completely purified," Radha said, shining with happiness.

"Please allow Me to bathe in Your lake every day, O Radha!" Krishna pleaded, kneeling before Radha and Radha Kunda. From that time Radha and Krishna have performed Their most enchanting pastimes at Radha Kunda every day. Vaishnavas always meditate upon these pastimes. Therefore Rupa Goswami wrote in Upadeshamrita, "Pure love for Krishna awakens in one who bathes even once in the sacred waters of Radha Kunda."

The glory of Radha Kunda is that anyone who, even once in life, experiences the love Radha feels for Krishna, figuratively described as "bathing in Radha Kunda," immediately becomes a pure devotee of Krishna and attains gopi-prema.

Sri Radha Kunda is non-different from Srimati Radharani and is therefore very dear to Sri Krishna. Radha Kunda has eight kunjas on its eight sides, belonging to the eight principal gopis. Sri Radha and Krishna perform Their midday pastimes at Radha Kunda. It is situated beside Govardhan, in one of its sections.

In the eleventh verse of Upadeshamrita, Srila Rupa Goswami says that one who bathes in Radha Kunda attains the rarest prema. But what does this mean? Does it mean simply coming and dipping into the water? No. It means bathing with great faith in one's perfected spiritual body. The true Radha Kunda is beyond the perception of material senses, mind, and intelligence. By these means we cannot even approach Radha Kunda, although we may think we are standing beside it or bathing in it. Radha Kunda, being the Lord's abode, is perceived only by transcendental senses free from material contamination.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati always expressed the deepest reverence for Sri Radha Kunda when he came there during Vraja Mandala Parikrama. He never allowed himself to bathe in Sri Radha Kunda. Knowing that Radha Kunda is non-different from Srimati Radharani Herself, his eternal Mistress, he trembled at the thought of casually entering Radha Kunda with his feet and body, as many people do. Since one enters the water feet first and immerses the whole body, he could not permit himself to place his feet "upon the head" of Srimati Radharani, considering this an unthinkable offense. With great reverence he bowed to Radha Kunda from a distance, then approached its sacred water and respectfully placed three drops upon his head. In this way he bathed in Radha Kunda.

Sri Radha Kunda is the lake of Srimati Radhika's love for Sri Krishna. It is the embodiment of Her love and is therefore as dear to Sri Krishna as Srimati Radharani Herself, as the manifestation of Her love. The appearance festival of Radha Kunda is also called Bahulashtami.

events.name: Dipavali / Dipa Dana
events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Dipavali / Dipa Dana. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
Dipavali, also called Diwali or Dipa Dana, is one of India's most joyful and colorful festivals. It is also known as the Festival of Lights. Literally, Dipavali means "a row of lights." It symbolizes the journey from darkness, or ignorance, to knowledge; the victory of truth over falsehood; and the victory of good over evil. Dipavali has been celebrated in India for more than seven thousand years. The festival marks the end of one season, the rainy season, and the beginning of the next, winter. It was the time when peasants and farmers gathered the harvest, and merchants raised their sails to travel and trade in other countries after the rains. This is one of the main reasons Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity and abundance, is honored at this time.

On Diwali certain traditions are observed, and each carries a spiritual meaning. The home and the body are put in order. The body is purified through meditation. Wearing new clothes represents dressing the inner self in something new. One also observes restraint from the five vices of life: passion or lust, anger, greed, attachment, and ego. In this way one begins the purification of thoughts, words, actions, and relationships. Lighting the home with colorful lamps means that the mind, the light of understanding, should be present. The clay lamps, called dipas, represent the body, which is a combination of the five elements: fire, water, air, space, and earth. This body is temporary and is given to us only for a time.

The flame of the dipa represents the soul, the atma, which, upon attaining a constant connection with the Supreme Soul, Paramatma, gives off bright and sparkling rays. The oil represents a priceless component: spiritual knowledge. To keep the flame always burning means to remain always conscious: "I am light, eternally connected with the Supreme Light." On this festival people strive to awaken from the deep sleep of ignorance and to be connected with the Supreme Light, God.

Dipavali is also a time to settle accounts, both financial and karmic. Bathing by starlight before sunrise is accepted as bathing in the sacred Ganga; thus purification of soul and body is an auspicious way to begin the day. This cleansing and focus on everything new symbolize casting off the sins of the past year and welcoming the hopes of the coming year. Saris woven with golden threads symbolize the Golden Age, Satya-yuga, in the Vedic cycle of time, an age of purity and harmony. Old clothes are cast aside as a reminder that the old world of the Iron Age, Kali-yuga, will end and give way to new life.

events.full_description:
A wonderful story is connected with the festival of Jahnu Saptami. Once, Jahnu Muni was sitting and chanting the Gayatri mantra when the Ganga rushed past him, following the chariot of King Bhagiratha in order to deliver his ancestors. The river washed away the paraphernalia that Jahnu Muni had set aside for achamana. Angered, the sage used his mystic power and drank the Ganga as if she were only a few drops of water.

Seeing that the Ganga was no longer flowing behind him, King Bhagiratha became anxious and began searching everywhere for her. At last he understood that Jahnu Muni had simply drunk the river, and he performed austerities to appease the sage. Being softened, Jahnu Muni released the Ganga from his ear. From that time the Ganga became known as Jahnavi, the daughter of Jahnu Muni.

On this day the Ganga is worshiped. Many people offer respects to their ancestors and bathe in the Ganga.

events.subject: Ганга Пуджа
events.name: Ganga Pudzha
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Ганга Пуджа". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Ganga Puja, also known as Ganga Dashahara, is the festival of worship of the sacred Ganga River. It is the appearance day of Mother Ganga, the day when the holy river descended from heaven to earth.

Goddess Ganga is the daughter of Himavat, king of the mountains, and his wife Mena. Ganga is the sister of Goddess Parvati, the consort of Shiva.

According to the Puranas, Ganga flows from the toe of Vishnu. At first she remained only in heaven, but later she was brought down to earth to bathe the ashes of King Sagara's sixty thousand sons.

Traditionally, many people gather on this day along the banks of this wonderful current of love. Priests from nearby temples step knee-deep into the water and offer the Ganga enormous lamps with oil wicks. People then cast flowers and garlands into the water and offer prayers to Ganga Devi, the goddess of the river.

The tradition of worshiping the Ganga is several thousand years old. According to ancient sacred sources such as Srimad-Bhagavatam, the Ganga is not merely a river but the energy of the great Viraja River that separates the material and spiritual worlds.

Ganga is the name of the sacred and most celebrated river. The holy Ganga is herself a temple. Ganga is the River of Purity, Knowledge, Unity, and Enlightenment given to us by the Creator. Knowledge overcomes darkness and ignorance. Dashahara means "that which purifies from the ten principal sins." It signifies removing darkness by bringing light. Traditionally, Ganga Dashahara is the day when the sacred river descends from heaven to earth to wash away our sins. It is a time when nature assists us.

Ganga Dashahara symbolizes purification of the soul and purification of our surroundings. This is an auspicious day to begin a cleaner life. Traditionally, a special puja is performed during these days for inner purification and the removal of deep negativity. Ganga Puja is intended to create a pure and positive influence in life.

Several ancient accounts tell how Ganga descended from heaven.

Once the great King Bhagiratha came to Mount Himavan to perform severe austerities. Desiring to save his ancestors, who had not attained heaven, he spent a thousand years in penance. After a thousand celestial years, the great river, Goddess Ganga herself, appeared before him in bodily form and asked what he desired. The king replied that his ancestors would not receive a place in heaven until she bathed their remains with her waters. Hearing the king's words, Ganga, honored by the whole world, said that she would fulfill his desire. Yet the force of her fall from heaven would be impossible for the earth to bear; only Lord Shiva could restrain her waters.

Hearing this, King Bhagiratha went to Mount Kailash and began worshiping Shiva. Pleased by the king's austerities, Bhagavan promised to receive Ganga when she fell from heaven. Thus Ganga, daughter of Himavan, king of the mountains, descended into this world.

As Ganga fell from the sky, Shiva received her upon his head so that her weight would not destroy the earth. From his head she flowed downward in seven streams. The turbulent river flooded the fields of Rishi Jahnu, who angrily drank her waters. Appeased by King Bhagiratha, he later released them through his ear. Finally, merging with the ocean, Ganga entered the subterranean realm of Patala.

According to another account, Ganga is the water Brahma used to wash Vishnu's feet. After bathing the great toe of Vamana, an avatar of Vishnu, Brahma collected the water in a vessel, where it became Ganga. Therefore the river is called Vishnu-padodbhava, "she who arises from the feet of Vishnu." By entering Brahma's vessel of water used to wash Vishnu's feet, Ganga received even greater power from Brahma and Vishnu, and her purifying potency increased.

"O Ganga, the world will receive auspiciousness through your movement over the earth among human beings. Be fearless."

Standing in Ganga's divine presence, the celestial beings became more powerful than they had been even after drinking nectar. Thus they were able to resist the attacks of demons and sustain and revive righteousness upon the earth. Vishnu is all-pervading throughout the three worlds: earth, heaven, and Patala. With Brahma's assistance, He bestowed Ganga's presence upon the heavens.

"O Ganga, you possess pure vibrations that cleanse all sin.

"O Ganga, your vow to purify everyone and everything began when Brahma washed Vishnu's feet with your water. The divine powers of Brahma and Vishnu are your wings. By your graceful glance, sattvic qualities develop in the celestial beings. You protect within me the aspect of Sat-Chit-Ananda."

events.subject: Гопаштами (Гоштхаштами)
events.name: Gopashtami (Goshtkhashtami)
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Гопаштами (Гоштхаштами)". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
The festival of Gopashtami, or Goshthashtami, is observed as the day when Lord Sri Krishna became a true cowherd. Until then He had been allowed to herd only calves, but on this day He became a gopa, a cowherd boy. This festival is also a festival of the cows.

In Gopala Champu, Jiva Goswami tells how on Gopashtami, the eighth day of the month of Kartika, when Krishna was six years old, His parents first entrusted Him with herding calves. Nanda Maharaj personally selected gentle calves for Krishna and gave Him a horn, a staff, a rope, and a flute. Mother Yashoda brought Him beautiful wooden shoes and a parasol to protect Him from the sun. Krishna accepted the staff, flute, and horn, but He was very surprised by Mother Yashoda's gifts.

"Mother, why do I need a parasol and shoes?" He asked. Yashoda replied that the parasol was needed to shield Him from the scorching sun, and the shoes to protect His feet from sharp stones on the road. She instructed Balarama to hold the parasol over Krishna and to watch carefully that He always kept His shoes on.

Then Krishna asked, "Mother, will you also give shoes and parasols to each of My calves? They will be walking on the same roads as I do, under the same sun. If so, I will not be able to hold a parasol over each of them; you must also give people to carry those parasols." Mother Yashoda answered that this is not done: calves do not walk with parasols and shoes. Then little Krishna looked at her very seriously and said, "If My calves are without shoes and parasols, then I will also be without shoes and without a parasol, because My duty is not to care for Myself, but to care for the calves."

Thus Gopashtami is the day when Krishna, who had previously herded calves, was first allowed to herd cows. In His honor, and while thinking of Him, cows should be worshiped with the ten upacharas and the mantra "om gave namah." On this day people usually observe fasting and perform Go Puja, worshiping cows as sacred animals. Thousands gather in temples to pray to Krishna and Go Lakshmi, because the nourishing cow has always been an essential support of life, especially in tropical countries.

On Gopashtami it is customary to clean the goshala, wash and decorate the cows. These sacred animals are shown special honor. Their horns are colored with turmeric, they are decorated with beautiful flower garlands and ribbons, and sindur is applied to them. They are then offered various items, most often special leaves and grasses, fruits, and rice. In some places a young boy is dressed as Krishna in remembrance of His pastimes, and it seems as if Krishna Himself is running through all the villages, blessing the devotees with His darshan.

In the Harivamsha Purana, Indra glorifies Krishna for becoming the beloved cowherd of the cows, proclaiming, "People too will glorify Him as Govinda." Krishna is Govinda, the protector of the cows. May Sri Govindadev, the playful Lord and leader of the cowherds, be our shelter.

events.full_description:
On the full moon of the month of Ashadha, Guru Purnima is traditionally celebrated. This day is also known as Vyasa Purnima, the day of honoring the sage Veda Vyasa, the original Guru, who classified the Vedas and recorded the eighteen Puranas and the Mahabharata. On this day, disciples and followers offer puja and arati to the Guru.

Worship unto you, O Vyasa, who possess wisdom, whose eyes are like lotus petals. You are the one who lit the lamp of knowledge, filled with the oil of the Mahabharata.

The Sanskrit root gu means darkness or ignorance, and ru means the overcoming of that darkness. Therefore the guru is one who dispels and destroys the darkness of our ignorance. Only one who completely removes the darkness of our ignorance and maya, and leads us to Bhagavan, is the true Guru.

Just as teachers in an ordinary school open knowledge to students and lead them from ignorance to knowledge, the spiritual Guru leads his disciple-children from darkness to light, from unreality to Reality.

In addition to giving help, instruction, and guidance on the path, the Guru sheds light, understanding, upon the wisdom of the scriptures. The Mundaka Upanishad calls such a Guru shrotriya, one who knows the true meaning of the scriptures.

The Guru plays an essential role in a person's life. In truth, the Guru is father, brother, friend, and more: the Guru is Ishvara Himself, revealing Truth to His devotees and helping them overcome avidya.

Meditation on the Guru is the source of meditation. The feet of the Guru are the foundation of puja. The speech of the Guru is the hidden mantra. The mercy of the Guru is the gift of liberation.

The Guru always helps his child, whether the difficulty is loss of enthusiasm, the struggles of life, or not understanding something. The Guru is love and compassion itself. Restrictions: during this period, which is also the final month of Chaturmasya, devotees traditionally avoid urad dal / black gram. The heart of the vrata is not external austerity alone, but remembrance of Lord Damodara and a sincere effort to deepen devotion throughout the Karttik period.

events.subject: Начало Радха Говинда Джхулан Ятры
events.name: Nachalo Radkha Govinda Dzhkhulan Yatry
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Начало Радха Говинда Джхулан Ятры". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
During the celebration of the swing festival, one of the most famous festivals held in Vrindavan, small Deities of Radha and Krishna are moved from the altar to beautifully decorated swings in the temple room in most of Vrindavan's five thousand temples. Every evening, after the traditional service, the Deities are gently swung.

Everyone may take part in Jhulan Yatra. Guests and devotees offer the Deities flower petals, fruits, and sweets, offer their prayers, and swing Their Lordships while the others sing Hare Krishna and other prayers glorifying Sri Sri Radha and Krishna. These days are also a very good time to donate for the Janmashtami festival and to feed Vaishnavas with prasadam.

In Vrindavan the festival begins on the third day of the bright half of the month of Shravana (July-August) and continues until the full moon of the same month. The main celebrations take place in the temples of Banke Bihari and Radha Raman, in the Dwarkadhish temple in Mathura, and in the Larili Lal temple in Varshana.

The earliest ceremony begins in the Banke Bihari temple, where the Lord is swung on a golden swing. On the first day of Jhulan Yatra, the streets around the temple are so crowded that cars and rickshaws can move only on the main roads. Some devotees must wait for the last arati, held at midnight, because attempting to enter the temple earlier, when hundreds of thousands of local residents are trying to participate in this wonderful festival, seems almost impossible.

At this time in India the rainy season is underway, and therefore it is very hot despite the cool rain. When so much water is pouring from the sky, the last thing one wants is more water, even if water is needed for cooling. Since the air is heavy and humid, the greatest pleasure at this time is a breeze. Therefore, wishing to please Krishna and Srimati Radharani, devotees swing Them, creating a gentle breeze through the motion.

The swings are decorated with vines, jasmine (malati), which blossoms at this time, and garlands. Sometimes rose water is sprayed around the swing for the pleasure of the Divine Couple, Sri Sri Radha-Krishna.

During the sacred month of Shravana, similar festivals are held in other parts of India. For example, in Jagannath Puri, for the pleasure of the Deity Madan Mohan (Krishna), who is considered non-different from Lord Jagannath, the festival is held for seven days, beginning on the tenth day of the bright half of Shravana and continuing until the first day of the dark half. Sri Madan Mohan, together with Lakshmi and Vishvadhatri, is placed on decorated wooden swings in a special pavilion. Until late at night the devotees swing the Lord, while special temple brahmanas sing songs and narrate the pastimes of Lord Krishna. On the full moon day, Jhulan Purnima, the appearance day of Lord Balarama is celebrated with great solemnity.

In different temples of Vrindavan, Jhulan Yatra lasts from one to thirteen days. Traditionally, many Deities during this period, up to Balaram Purnima, are dressed in various outfits that include green colors.

By the mercy of Srila Prabhupada, Jhulan Yatra festivals are now held in ISKCON temples all over the world. Usually the festival lasts three days. But whether it lasts one, five, or thirteen days, its purpose is to give pleasure to the Lord and His intimate associates, and also to all the devotees who receive the opportunity to participate in personal service to the Lord.

Jhulan Yatra and the other festivals held throughout the year are not merely traditional rituals. They remind us of the Lord's pastimes beyond the material world, in spiritual reality. The Lord descends into the material world in the form of the Deity to give conditioned souls, who cannot see His eternal spiritual form, the opportunity to serve Him and participate in His pastimes.

events.subject: Праздник Джаганнатхи Мишры
events.name: Prazdnik Dzhagannatkhi Mishry
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Праздник Джаганнатхи Мишры". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Jagannath Mishra was born in a brahmana family in the Bengali village of South Dhaka, now in the Sylhet district of Bangladesh. In his youth, Jagannath Mishra came to Navadvipa for study, where he married Shachidevi, the daughter of the renowned scholar-brahmana Nilambara Chakravarti of Navadvipa. After that he settled permanently on the bank of the Ganga in Mayapur. Jagannath Mishra was a poor brahmana and maintained his family by collecting alms. He and his wife Shachidevi had eight daughters, all of whom died at an early age. The couple then devoted themselves to raising their two surviving sons, Vishvarupa and Vishvambhara. Vishvambhara was the tenth and youngest child. Later He became known as Nimai Pandit, and after accepting sannyasa, as Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

Before appearing as Lord Chaitanya, Sri Krishna asked the following devotees to appear on earth: Sri Shachidevi, Jagannath Mishra, Madhavendra Puri, Keshava Bharati, Ishvara Puri, Advaita Acharya, Srivas Pandit, Acharyaratna, Vidyanidhi, and Thakur Haridas.

Overwhelmed with joy at the birth of his dear son, Sri Jagannath Mishra held a great festival and a lavish feast on the day after the child's birth, now known as the festival of Jagannath Mishra. Devis from the heavenly planets took the forms of brahmana ladies and came to his home to worship the infant. Following traditional rites, they offered gifts to Nimai, touched His forehead with kusha grass, and showered Him with rice mixed with turmeric. Malini, the wife of Srivas Thakur, came there with other joyful women to worship the child, offering Him vermilion, turmeric, oil, puffed rice, bananas, and coconuts.

Sita Thakurani, the wife of Advaita Acharya, gave the Lord the name Nimai because He had been born beneath a neem tree. It is said that neem protects from witches and sorcerers, and that evil spirits cannot remain near such a tree. Thus Sita Thakurani gave the Lord the name Nimai so that nothing could harm Him. Others began calling Him Gaurahari, the Golden Lord, because He radiated an extraordinary effulgence and His complexion was like molten gold.

In this way Shachidevi and Jagannath Mishra received a son who was none other than the husband of the goddess of fortune, and all their desires were fulfilled. In their home there was always sufficient grain and money. Seeing their beloved child, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, they became happier day by day. Since then, this festival has been observed each year by honoring delicious prasadam.

events.subject: Punar Yatra of Sri Jagannathdev
events.name: Punar Yatra of Sri Jagannathdev
events.short_description: Return car festival of Sri Jagannathdev after the stay at Gundicha temple.
events.full_description:
After the Lord's stay at the Gundicha temple, the return journey is celebrated as Punar Yatra, also known as Bahuda Yatra. Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra, and Subhadra Devi return from Gundicha to Sri Mandir on Their chariots.

On the return path the Deities are traditionally offered poda pitha, a special cake made from rice, lentils, jaggery, and coconut. Near the end of the festival the Lord is dressed in golden ornaments in the celebrated Suna Besha, and the sweet drink Adhara Pana is offered.

The return also carries a tender dramatic mood: Lakshmi Devi, having been left behind at the main temple, expresses loving displeasure before the Lord is finally welcomed back to His jeweled throne.

events.subject: Рамачандра Виджайотсава
events.name: Ramachandra Vidzhayotsava
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Рамачандра Виджайотсава". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
On this day Lord Ramachandra heard from Hanuman that he had seen and heard news of Sita on the island of Lanka. In honor of this news, Lord Ramachandra held a festival and then set out for Sri Lanka.

On the day of Ramachandra Vijayotsava, one may perform puja to Lord Ramachandra and then feed the Vaishnavas in His honor. This festival is especially popular in northern India, where large paper forms of the demon Ravana are burned amid loud songs glorifying the victory of Lord Ramachandra.

events.subject: Ratha Yatra of Sri Jagannathdev
events.name: Beginning of Ratha Yatra
events.short_description: The chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra, and Subhadra Devi begins on Vamana Gaura Dvitiya.
events.full_description:
Ratha Yatra is celebrated every year in Puri, the sacred temple city of Odisha. Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra, Subhadra Devi, and Sudarshan are brought from Sri Mandir in a solemn procession and placed upon immense, brightly decorated chariots. Thousands of devotees draw the chariots along the Bada Danda toward the Gundicha temple.

This festival is one of the most merciful public forms of darshan. The Lord, who normally remains upon the altar, comes out to be seen by everyone. Saints and scriptures glorify the sight of Lord Jagannath on His chariot, and even touching the chariot or its ropes is praised as spiritually auspicious.

The three chariots are built anew each year. Lord Jagannath rides on Nandighosha, Lord Balabhadra on Taladhvaja, and Subhadra Devi on Darpadalana. After the Pahandi procession, the chariots are pulled, beginning with Balabhadra's chariot, then Subhadra's, and finally Lord Jagannath's chariot.

In the Gaudiya tradition this day is also deeply connected with Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's ecstatic participation in the Ratha Yatra of Puri.

events.subject: Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka
events.name: Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka
events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
In the Skanda Purana (2.2.42), Sri Krishna Pushya Abhisheka is described as one of the principal festivals held for the Deities of Jagannath, Baladeva, and Subhadra in Puri, Orissa. That chapter gives a detailed description of the ceremony for this festival. Srila Prabhupada once explained its meaning to his disciples in this way: "Krishna was simply a plaything in the hands of the gopis, and so one day the gopis decided to decorate Him. Pushya Abhisheka means a ceremony of opulently decorating the Deity with flowers, jewels, and garments. Afterward there should be generous feasting and a procession through the streets of the towns and villages, so that all the citizens may see how beautiful Sri Krishna is."

The Hari-bhakti-vilasa says that on this day, during the morning puja, the Deity of Krishna or the Shalagram should be anointed with pure ghee. After bathing, the Deity is beautifully and richly dressed, splendidly decorated with jewels, and adorned with luxurious garlands of fresh flowers. Devotees also offer butter to Krishna. Then generous feasts are arranged, and the Deity is brought out in procession through the streets so the whole world may see how beautiful and perfect Lord Sri Krishna is.

events.subject: Снана Ятра
events.name: Snana Yatra
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "Снана Ятра". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Snana Yatra falls on the full moon of the month of Jyeshtha. According to the Skanda Purana, Lord Jagannath appeared on this very day.

No fewer than 200,000 pilgrims gather in the temple complex on Jyeshtha Purnima to attend the bathing ceremony of the Deities, which takes place on the Snana Vedi, the special bathing altar. It is believed that receiving darshan of Lord Jagannath on the day of Snana Yatra purifies one from all sins.

During the solemn ceremony, the Deities of Jagannath, Baladeva, and Subhadra are brought out of the Jagannath temple and placed on a special platform. Then, while mantras are chanted, the Deities are bathed with water from 108 pots, drawn from the well in the northern part of the temple known as the Golden Well.

In the evening, after the bathing ritual is completed, Jagannath and Baladeva are dressed with elephant masks representing Ganesha.

After this the Deities are dressed in ivory-colored garments and taken to the "sick room," where They remain for two weeks. During this period, called Anavasara, the Deities are said to suffer from a cold and are treated by the physician of the king of Puri. It is said that by Ayurvedic methods the physician cures the Deities.

All the paint is also washed from the Deities, and They are painted anew. On the day of Ratha Yatra the Deities are ceremonially brought out of the temple and placed on Their chariots, so that, accompanied by crowds of devotees, They may be taken to the Gundicha temple.

The Gundicha temple is located three kilometers from the famous Jagannath temple and has special importance in the worship of Lord Jagannath. Throughout the year the Gundicha temple stands empty, except for nine days in the Hindu month of Ashadha, when, during the Ratha Yatra festival, the Deities of Jagannath, Baladeva, and Subhadra are brought there from the Jagannath temple on huge chariots in a solemn procession. According to legend, the original temple at this site was built by Gundicha, the wife of King Indradyumna, who founded the Jagannath temple.

The Skanda Purana says that the first person to perform the Snana Yatra ceremony was King Indradyumna, the founder of the Jagannath temple.

events.subject: Sri Balarama Rasa-yatra
events.name: Sri Balarama Rasa-yatra
events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Sri Balarama Rasa-yatra. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
Lord Balarama is non-different from Sri Krishna, and at the same time every part of His transcendental body longs to serve Sri Krishna. Therefore Guru is non-different from Balarama. Sri Krishna is the Supreme Enjoyer, and all others are His servants. Sri Balarama manifests the Dham and all the incarnations of the Lord for the service of Sri Krishna. In Krishna-lila He serves through His consort Yoga-maya.

Sri Balarama performed rasa-lila with His own gopis. The gopis of Sri Balarama relate to Sri Krishna in dasya-rasa, and the gopis of Sri Krishna also relate to Lord Balarama in dasya-rasa. When Sri Balarama performs this lila, in the depth of His heart He offers everything to Sri Krishna.

"To please the gopis, Lord Balarama stayed in Vrindavan for two full months: Chaitra (March-April) and Vaishakha (April-May). During those two months He remained among the gopis, and every night He met them in the forests of Vrindavan to satisfy their desire for conjugal love. In this way Balarama also enjoyed the rasa dance with the gopis." Srila Prabhupada, Krishna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Volume 2, page 118, "Lord Balarama Visits Vrindavan."

events.subject: Sri Krishna Vasanta Rasa

events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Sri Krishna Vasanta Rasa. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
Sri Krishna Vasanta Rasa resembles the autumn rasa dance, with one special difference: it takes place in spring, and everyone is dressed in yellow. Lord Krishna's spring rasa dance is performed at night under the full moon. Playing His flute on the bank of the Yamuna in Vrindavan, Krishna captivates the hearts of Srimati Radhika and all the gopis of Vraja, and they hurry to meet Him.

On this night, devotees traditionally leave pots of sweet rice, payasam, for the Lord's enjoyment during His rasa dance.

In the course of that search, He learned that Vishvarupa had been in Pandharpur. When Mahaprabhu reached Pandharpur, He heard that His brother, who had accepted sannyasa much earlier, had also visited that place and that it was the last place of his stay on earth. events.subject: Sri Nityananda Prabhu
events.name: Sri Nityananda Prabhu Appearance
events.short_description: Appearance day festival for Sri Nityananda Prabhu. The calendar matches it by the configured tithi rule.
events.full_description:
The great saint Vrindavan Das Thakur says that this festival is filled with unlimited mercy. Sri Nityananda came as the principal associate of Lord Chaitanya. By serving Gauranga with complete self-giving, He teaches us what can make us truly happy. This is expressed in His very name: "eternal bliss." By worshiping Lord Nityananda, one attains love and devotion to the lotus feet of Krishna.

Nityananda was born in 1474 in the village of Ekachakra in Radhadesh. As a child, He constantly played with His friends, imitating the pastimes of Krishna, and in this way He spent the first twelve years of His life. On the day in 1486 when Sri Chaitanya was born in Navadvipa, Nityananda cried out in joy. After that, by divine arrangement, Nitai set out on pilgrimage to various holy places throughout North and South India in order to purify them from the sins left there by pilgrims. He remained engaged in this way until His twentieth year. On the path He seemingly met Madhavendra Puri by chance and accepted him as His Guru. For many days Nityananda traveled in the company of Madhavendra Puri, discussing Krishna's pastimes with him.

While Lord Gaurachandra was growing up in Navadvipa, Nityananda remained in Vrindavan. Sri Nityananda thought to Himself, "Chaitanya lives in Navadvipa, but His divine glory remains hidden. As soon as He decides to reveal His divinity, I will immediately go to Navadvipa and fulfill my role in serving Him." Only in 1506 did Lord Nityananda set foot on the blessed land of Nadia. The joy of the meeting between Lord Vishvambhar and Lord Nityananda cannot be expressed in words; tears of joy flowed constantly from Their eyes.

After Lord Chaitanya accepted sannyasa and settled in Jagannath Puri, absorbed in meditation on Krishna's pastimes, He asked Lord Nityananda to preach in Bengal on His behalf. There Nityananda manifested Himself as the savior of the most fallen. He gave Lord Chaitanya's mercy even to the most hardened wrongdoers. For Nityananda there is no one "unworthy of mercy". He bestows it upon everyone; one need only begin to serve Him. Bhaktivinod Thakur describes a good way to serve Him:

"In the town of Nadia, on the island of Godrum, Lord Nityananda opened the marketplace of the Holy Name for the deliverance of all fallen souls. O people, believe this! By the order of Lord Gauranga I have come to beg you, O brothers: chant the name of Krishna, worship Krishna, and give Krishna to others!"

The year of Nityananda Prabhu's disappearance is not known with certainty; according to one tradition, it was 1541.

Nityananda Prabhu is non-different from Krishna and possesses all six opulences. The only difference is Their bodies and moods. Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the original Guru of the universe, whose very principle of life is service to the Lord.

In the role of servant, Nityananda expands Himself to become the Lord's shoes, His garments, His seat, His bed, the Dham, and His abode. In the material world Sri Nityananda Prabhu expands Himself as Maha Vishnu, Garbhodakashayi Vishnu, and Kshirodakashayi Vishnu; He creates and maintains the entire cosmic manifestation.

In the role of teacher, Lord Nityananda comes into the material world to show by His own example how to serve the Lord with pure devotion. All true spiritual teachers are representatives, manifestations of the mercy of Nityananda Prabhu. He fulfills the desire of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu: to give Krishna consciousness even to the most fallen and unqualified.

events.name: Appearance of Narottamy Dasa Tkhakura
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Нароттамы Даса Тхакура". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Narottam Das Thakur was an embodiment of the Gaudiya teaching. He transmitted love of God through the poetry we know, and just as poetically he embodied that love in his own life. He was a perfect devotee, the ideal of a divine messenger, possessing the qualities described by the Six Goswamis whenever their pens touched palm leaves. The essence of Gaudiya Vaishnava philosophy is reflected in all his songs and ideals. Two important events preceded the appearance of Narottam Das Thakur: first, the appearance in this world of Lokanath Goswami, and second, the prediction of his birth by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

As stated in Narottam's writings, he outlived Jiva Goswami and his best friend Ramachandra Kaviraj. Just as he deeply felt separation from Mahaprabhu and from Radha and Krishna, he also acutely felt separation from his exalted contemporaries. Narottam's biographers always describe him in a state of divine bliss and sorrow, which, according to Vaishnava doctrine, awakens the highest spiritual feelings. Describing Narottam's condition, they write that "he constantly watered the earth with streams of tenderness flowing from his pious eyes." With unparalleled intensity he longed for God and His associates.

At last Narottam could no longer bear love in separation and joined the Lord in the spiritual world. In the house of Ganga Narayan Chakravarti in Murshidabad, he entered trance, completely absorbed in the lilas of Radha and Krishna. This continued for several days, convincing many that Narottam was about to leave this world. Yet at that solemn moment, some of his most zealous opponents, caste brahmanas, began mocking him. "Just look," they cried, "all his life he initiated brahmanas, though he was only a low-born shudra, and now he is dying as a shudra." Ganga Narayan Chakravarti could not bear these slanders and began praying to his guru: "Please return. Show them that they are simply fools." At that moment Narottam's body shone, and a golden brahmana thread mystically appeared on him. Seeing this miracle, the caste brahmanas immediately recognized their mistake and surrendered at Narottam's feet, begging forgiveness.

Narottam-vilasa tells a somewhat different story. Narottam asked his disciples to take him to Budhari and then to Gambhila so that he could bathe in the Ganga. Suddenly he was seized by a severe fever and understood that he might soon die. Without delay, he ordered his disciples to prepare a funeral pyre. Naturally, this was not easy for them, but they obeyed their guru's will. Narottam then sat silently for three days and left his body before many witnesses and disciples.

When his soul departed, the disciples seated his body on a decorated seat in the middle of the prepared pyre. It was then that the critical brahmanas began speaking maliciously in the presence of Ganga Narayan and other faithful followers of Narottam. Ganga Narayan could not tolerate it and prayed to Narottam to return and show mercy to these misguided brahmanas. At that moment Narottam's eyes opened, and he said, "Radha-Krishna-Chaitanya!" Moreover, his body shone like the sun, and the astonished brahmanas changed their view. All who witnessed this revival surrendered at Narottam's lotus feet. He embraced them all, bestowing precious bhakti upon them. He instructed them to study devotional literature under the guidance of Ganga Narayan Chakravarti, and then he left that place, wishing to meditate alone. During the last several months he displayed signs of ecstasy and constantly experienced separation from Sri Sri Radha and Krishna.

Narottam Das Thakur wrote many songs, including Gauranga Bolite Habe, Radha Krishna Prana Mora, and Je Anilo Prema Dhana.

events.subject: День явления Нимбарки Ачарьи
events.name: Appearance of Nimbarki Achari
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Нимбарки Ачарьи". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Nimbarka Acharya was a great ascetic. He wrote many books on Dvaitadvaita-vada and spent most of his life surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krishna, in a place called Nimbagrama near Govardhan in Vrindavan.

Nimbarka Acharya belongs to the Kumar sampradaya. He is believed to have lived around the eleventh or twelfth century. He was born in present-day Murgarapattam in the southern Dravidian province. He was the son of Aruni and Jayanti, a very pious brahmana family. His parents named him Niyamananda. Aruna Muni and Jayanti Devi performed the sacred-thread ceremony for their son and sent him to the rishi-kula to study the Vedas, Vedanga, darshana, and other branches of learning. Niyamanandacharya mastered the scriptures in a short time. He was a great genius, and people came from all parts of India to see this remarkable boy.

During his stay in Nimbagrama, a philosophical debate took place between Nimbarka Acharya and a great Jain pandit, from which Nimbarka emerged as the unquestioned victor. The Jain, whose pride had been wounded, refused to dine with his successful opponent, saying that the sun had supposedly already set and therefore he would not take any food at such a time. Hearing these words, Nimbarka, by his mystic power, made the sun appear from a neem tree. The astonished Jain then accepted his hospitality. Thus it is said that the name Nimbarka or Nimbaditya was given to him because of this miracle. Literally, it means "the sun of the neem tree." Nimbarka was also known by the names Rishi Aruna and Haripriyacharya.

According to other sources, when Niyamanandacharya was a teenager, Brahma, the creator of the universe, came to the ashram of Aruna Muni disguised as a sannyasi. The sun was already setting. The muni was not at home. The sannyasi asked the muni's wife for food, but there was none. The muni's wife did not know what to say. When the sannyasi was about to leave, Niyamanandacharya said to his mother, "Dear mother, a sannyasi must not leave without being fed. We will have to suffer for violating atithi-dharma, the duty toward a guest." His mother replied, "Dear son, your father has gone out. I have neither fruit nor roots. Besides, there is no time to cook. It is sunset, and a sannyasi will not accept food after sunset."

Then Niyamanandacharya addressed the sannyasi: "I will quickly bring roots and fruits from the forest. I promise that the sun will not set until You have finished Your meal." Niyamanandacharya placed his Sudarshan Chakra on a neem tree in the ashram, where it shone like the sun. Brahma, who had taken the form of the sannyasi, was amazed by what he saw. Within a few minutes Nimbarka returned with roots and fruits and gave them to his mother, who served the sannyasi with deep devotion. As soon as the sannyasi finished his meal, Nimbarka removed the Sudarshan Chakra from the neem tree. At once it became dark. One quarter of the night had already passed. The sannyasi, who was Brahma himself, gave the boy the name Nimbarka: nim means neem tree, and arka means Surya, the sun. From that time he was known as Sri Nimbarkacharya.

Nimbarka Acharya is considered an incarnation of Lord Hari's weapon, the Sudarshan Chakra. He was a true embodiment of mercy, piety, love, kindness, generosity, and other divine qualities.

events.subject: День явления Пурушоттамы Даса Тхакура
events.name: Appearance of Purushottamy Dasa Tkhakura
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Пурушоттамы Даса Тхакура". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
"Sadashiva Kaviraj was extraordinarily fortunate. His son was Sri Purushottama Das. He never identified himself with the material body. Sri Nityananda always resided in his heart." (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya 5.741-742)

Purushottama Das Thakur was a Vaishnava saint who lived in Bengal in the first half of the sixteenth century. He was one of the associates of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and one of the intimate companions of Nityananda Prabhu. Purushottama Das belongs to the group of twelve saints known as the dvadasha-gopalas. He is also known for formulating various styles of kirtan singing. The Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 11.38-39) states that Sadashiva Kaviraj and his son Purushottama Das were the twenty-third and twenty-fourth among the close associates of Nityananda. He was also the tenth of the twelve Gopalas. From birth, Purushottama Das was engaged in devotional service to the lotus feet of Nityananda Prabhu, and he was also a constant participant in the childhood pastimes of Lord Krishna.

Purushottama Thakur lived in Sukhasagar, Bengal. Some say that Purushottama's family name was Nagar, while others say that Nagar was the name of the district where he lived. Because five villages, Beledanga, Beligram, Sukhanagar, Magasapota, and Pal Para, are very close to one another, that area is sometimes called Nagaradesh. Purushottama Thakur had three principal disciples: Sri Madhavacharya, Sri Yadavacharya, and Devakinandana Prabhu. All three came from brahmana families. Later, Madhavacharya became the husband of Ganga Devi, the daughter of Nityananda Prabhu. Devakinandana Das is known as the author of Vaishnava-vandana, a book glorifying the greatest Vaishnavas.

Purushottama Das eternally serves Balarama in the spiritual world, on Goloka, as a cowherd boy. A pushpa-samadhi of Purushottama Das Thakur is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.subject: День явления Радха Кунды, Снана Дана
events.name: Appearance of Radkha Kundy, Snana Dana
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Радха Кунды, Снана Дана". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
After killing a demon who had assumed the form of a bull, Krishna, exhilarated by His victory, came to meet Radhika. Seeing Krishna stained with the bull's blood, Radha forbade Him to approach Her. Krishna tried to explain that it had been a shape-shifting demon and that He was very happy and proud to have defeated it. But Radha remained firm. She reminded Krishna that the bull represents religion, and that killing a bull, like killing a cow, is a very grave sin. Radha said that until Krishna purified Himself of the sin of killing a bull, She would not meet with Him.

"What should I do?" Krishna pleaded. "You must bathe in all the holy tirthas," Radha replied. Krishna then mystically created a large hollow and called all the sacred waters of the universe to come there. The presiding deities of all the holy rivers and lakes appeared before Krishna and filled the lake with their waters. It became known as Shyama Kunda. After bathing in that lake, Krishna appeared before Radharani. But noticing that some pride in His victory still remained in Krishna's heart, Radha told Him, "It seems the consequences of Your sin are very heavy; even all the sacred tirthas of the universe could not purify You."

Then Radha and Her friends removed their bracelets and began digging another hollow beside Shyama Kunda with them. They worked for many hours. When it was ready, Radha stood at its edge, raised Her arms, and prema flowed from Her heart into the hollow, soon filling it to the brim. Deeply moved, Krishna entered the water of this lake and emerged transformed to meet Radha. "Now You are completely purified," Radha said, shining with happiness.

"Please allow Me to bathe in Your lake every day, O Radha!" Krishna pleaded, kneeling before Radha and Radha Kunda. From that time Radha and Krishna have performed Their most enchanting pastimes at Radha Kunda every day. Vaishnavas always meditate upon these pastimes. Therefore Rupa Goswami wrote in Upadeshamrita, "Pure love for Krishna awakens in one who bathes even once in the sacred waters of Radha Kunda."

The glory of Radha Kunda is that anyone who, even once in life, experiences the love Radha feels for Krishna, figuratively described as "bathing in Radha Kunda," immediately becomes a pure devotee of Krishna and attains gopi-prema.

Sri Radha Kunda is non-different from Srimati Radharani and is therefore very dear to Sri Krishna. Radha Kunda has eight kunjas on its eight sides, belonging to the eight principal gopis. Sri Radha and Krishna perform Their midday pastimes at Radha Kunda. It is situated beside Govardhan, in one of its sections.

In the eleventh verse of Upadeshamrita, Srila Rupa Goswami says that one who bathes in Radha Kunda attains the rarest prema. But what does this mean? Does it mean simply coming and dipping into the water? No. It means bathing with great faith in one's perfected spiritual body. The true Radha Kunda is beyond the perception of material senses, mind, and intelligence. By these means we cannot even approach Radha Kunda, although we may think we are standing beside it or bathing in it. Radha Kunda, being the Lord's abode, is perceived only by transcendental senses free from material contamination.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati always expressed the deepest reverence for Sri Radha Kunda when he came there during Vraja Mandala Parikrama. He never allowed himself to bathe in Sri Radha Kunda. Knowing that Radha Kunda is non-different from Srimati Radharani Herself, his eternal Mistress, he trembled at the thought of casually entering Radha Kunda with his feet and body, as many people do. Since one enters the water feet first and immerses the whole body, he could not permit himself to place his feet "upon the head" of Srimati Radharani, considering this an unthinkable offense. With great reverence he bowed to Radha Kunda from a distance, then approached its sacred water and respectfully placed three drops upon his head. In this way he bathed in Radha Kunda.

Sri Radha Kunda is the lake of Srimati Radhika's love for Sri Krishna. It is the embodiment of Her love and is therefore as dear to Sri Krishna as Srimati Radharani Herself, as the manifestation of Her love. The appearance festival of Radha Kunda is also called Bahulashtami.

events.subject: День явления Рагхунанданы Тхакура
events.name: Appearance of Ragkhunandany Tkhakura
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Рагхунанданы Тхакура". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
The image shows the murti of little Raghunandan in his mother's arms at his birthplace, Sri Khanda.

Once, the physician Mukunda Das was called to see a patient, and he asked his younger son, Raghunandan, to offer the family Deity Gopinath the raja-bhoga. Raghunandan prepared everything on time, carefully and with great devotion. After making the offering, he remembered his father's words: "Make sure the Deity eats." Ringing the bell, the boy said to the Deity Gopinath, "Eat! Eat!" Seeing that everything on the plate remained untouched, he began to weep bitterly. He was afraid of his father's anger because he had not been able to "feed the Deity." Then Gopinath could not restrain Himself and decided to fulfill the child's desire. He ate everything, leaving nothing behind.

When Mukunda returned, he asked what his son had done with Gopinath's maha-prasadam. Raghunandan replied that the Deity had eaten everything. Astonished, Mukunda asked his son to make another offering. Sitting in a hidden place, Mukunda watched the wondrous scene as Raghunandan offered laddus to Gopinath. But the Lord ate only half of a laddu, from which Mukunda understood that the Deity was still satisfied from the noon offering. Overwhelmed by what he had seen and filled with divine feeling, Mukunda embraced his son, a pure devotee.

Later, in Jagannath Puri, Lord Gauranga lovingly asked Mukunda Das, "Who was the father, and who was the son?" Mukunda replied, "I consider my own son, Raghunandan, to be my father, for through him I came to know the science of Krishna consciousness."

In Krishna-lila, Raghunandan is Kandarpa Manjari, or Pradyumna in the Chatur-vyuha. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.
