events.subject: Appearance of Shankaracharya
events.name: Appearance of Shankaracharya
events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Appearance of Shankaracharya. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
Sri Shankaracharya, respectfully known as Bhagavatpada Acharya, lived in the eighth century. He was the most celebrated philosopher of Advaita and profoundly influenced the development of Hinduism through his nondual philosophy. He proclaimed the greatness and importance of the Vedic scriptures, especially the Upanishads, discussed spiritual subjects through reason rather than dogma or ritualism, and gave new life to Hinduism at a time when Buddhism and Jainism were becoming increasingly influential. Many consider him an incarnation of Lord Shiva on this planet.

Biography of Shankaracharya

Shankara was born in a small brahmana village in Kerala, southern India, to the virtuous brahmana Shivaguru and his wife Shivataraka. According to another account, his parents were named Vishvajit and Vishishta. They had long remained childless and prayed for a son while visiting shrines of Shiva. After one such pilgrimage, Shiva appeared to Shivaguru in a dream and offered him a choice: one hundred ordinary sons, or one great son whose life would be brief. Shivaguru chose the latter.

By the age of one, Shankara Acharya already spoke and wrote Sanskrit beautifully and performed miracles. Before everyone's eyes, an enormous cobra coiled around his neck transformed into a flower garland. By the age of five, when his father died, he had surpassed the local teachers. At seven he firmly resolved to become a wandering renunciant, a sannyasi. When eight-year-old Shankara was crossing a river with his mother, a river he had previously caused to flow closer to their home so that Shivataraka would not have to walk far for water, a huge crocodile seized him and refused to release him until his mother consented to his renunciation. That very day Shankara left home, promising his mother that he would return to her before her death.

Shankaracharya traveled north and reached the banks of the Narmada in central India, where many Shaiva shrines stood. Among the forest renunciants lived Govinda, a disciple of the Vedantist Gaudapada, whom Shankara accepted as his teacher.

Shankara's discipleship lasted at least two years. During this time he performed another miracle by collecting the overflowing waters of the Narmada in his begging bowl. Govinda then sent him farther north to the sacred city of Benares, where Shankara found his first disciple, Padmapada. From there he traveled to Badrinath in the Himalayas, where he wrote his celebrated commentaries on the Brahma-sutras, the Upanishads, and the Bhagavad-gita, as well as other treatises.

Shankaracharya debated with Vaishnavas, won numerous victories over Buddhists, and in the north competed with Shaiva Tantrics. Traveling throughout India and preaching his teaching, he consistently defeated his opponents, especially Buddhists. He established a community in Benares at one of the shrines for funeral rites on the bank of the Ganga.

There he also met a low-born chandala, the son of a shudra and a brahmana woman. Shankara initially wished to avoid contact with him, but the chandala convinced him of the equality of all living beings.

Shankaracharya criticized both "unorthodox" philosophical doctrines and those positions of the "orthodox" darshanas that offered explanations of the world and paths of liberation opposed to Vedanta. Shankara debated materialists who identified the Atman with the body, Jains who taught that the soul corresponds in size to the body, and Buddhists of all principal schools. In particular, he argued that the method by which Vijnanavadins rejected the reality of external objects could equally be used to reject the reality of the consciousness they accepted. Shankaracharya consistently distanced himself from simple illusionism.

Shankara Acharya not only preached but also established Vedantic monasteries, maths. The principal ones were founded in Dwarka in the west, Badrinath in the north, Puri in the east, Sringeri in the south, and Kanchi in the far south. He also established ten orders of Advaita renunciants.

Shankaracharya's first followers were his four disciples, each of whom, according to tradition, was appointed to lead one of the four monasteries he founded.

From the words of Sri Shankaracharya:

"Of the five qualities, Being, Consciousness, Bliss, name, and form, the first three belong to Brahman, while name and form belong to the world. The three aspects, Being, Consciousness, and Bliss, exist equally in the five elements, ether, air, fire, water, and earth, in the devas, animals, human beings, and so on, while names and forms differ. Therefore remain indifferent to names and forms, focus upon Being-Consciousness-Bliss, and constantly practice samadhi, identity with Brahman, within the heart or outside it."

events.name: Appearance of Shrimati Sity Devi
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Шримати Ситы Деви". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Srimati Sita Devi is the daughter of King Janaka and the consort of Lord Ramachandra. She is Lakshmiji herself, the eternal consort of Lord Narayana and the goddess of fortune. Her adoptive father found little Sita in the forest and immediately saw how much she resembled Lakshmi Devi. In time, however, he forgot this and loved her simply as his own daughter.

Once Sita Devi was walking in the forest with her friends. The girls tried in every way to reach a high branch, but they could not. Sita then went to the palace and quietly entered the room where the famous bow of Lord Shiva was kept, the bow with which he had fought Lord Vishnu. It normally took three thousand men to move the chariot on which that bow rested. Yet "little" Sita easily lifted the bow and quietly left the room. A guard standing nearby could hardly believe his eyes and immediately ran to the king. Sitaji shot down the branch and calmly returned the bow to its place. The ministers who gathered because of this extraordinary event told Janaka, "O king, Maha-Lakshmi lives in your house. All the signs show this clearly. How will you arrange Her marriage? If She is Lakshmiji, then you must find Sri Narayana, Her eternal Lord." Thus, later, Lord Ramachandra, Narayana Himself, came to the contest arranged by the father of Srimati Sita Devi and strung that bow. Such is the wondrous lila of the union of the eternal Divine Couple, Lord Narayana and Lakshmi Devi.

Just before His coronation, in obedience to the will of His father, Ramachandra went into exile for fourteen years together with Sita Devi and Lakshman. They lived in the forest, and there the lila took place in which Sita Devi was abducted by the wicked demon Ravana and held captive in Lanka. Searching for Sita, Rama besieged Lanka and killed Ravana. Yet before Rama accepted her back, Sita, to prove her fidelity to her Lord, had to pass through the trial of fire. Everyone stood still as Sita entered the blazing flames, but the tongues of fire could not harm Rama's faithful wife. In this way Sita proved her purity in thought, word, and deed.

After returning to Ayodhya, Rama learned that His subjects still suspected Sita of unfaithfulness and sent her to the forest. There she found shelter with the saintly sage Valmiki Muni, who raised her and Rama's two sons, Lava and Kusha. When the sons of Sita and Rama had grown, Valmiki returned her to Rama. But upon meeting Ramachandra, Sita asked her mother, the Earth, to receive her.

events.subject: День явления Шривасы Пандита
events.name: Appearance of Shrivasy Pandita
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День явления Шривасы Пандита". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
I bow down before Srila Srivas Pandit, the dear associate of Lord Sri Gauranga. By even a particle of the mercy of Srivas Thakur, one attains the purest love, rati, for Sri Gauranga. O Srivas! O Kirtanananda, embodiment of the bliss of hari-kirtan! O beloved of the entire assembly of the Lord's devotees! O maha-yogi, greatest of bhakti-yogis! O bhakta-rupa, embodiment of the ideal devotee, non-different from Sri Narada Goswami! I offer you my obeisances again and again.

Srivas Pandit lived in Navadvipa even before the appearance of Lord Chaitanya. He lived with his brothers Sri Rama, Sri Nidhi, and Sripati, chanting the names of Krishna with them, worshiping the Lord, and bathing three times daily in the Ganga. After meeting Sri Advaita Acharya Prabhu, they began studying the Bhagavatam and praying for the incarnation of the Supreme Lord. Malini, the wife of Srivas and a close friend of Shachi Devi, nursed little Nimai. When Lord Vishvambhar appeared, the hearts of all the devotees filled with parental affection, vatsalya-bhava. Gaurachandra loved Malini and Srivas as deeply as He loved His own parents.

The house of Srivas stood about two hundred meters from Nimai's house. It was a beautiful home with spacious rooms, surrounded by a high wall and by lush flowering gardens and groves. Every evening Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu and His closest associates enjoyed ecstatic kirtans there, tasting the moods of Vrindavan.

It was here that the angry Muslim ruler broke a mridanga while trying to stop the Sri Krishna sankirtan movement. Since then, the house of Srivas has been called Khol Bhanga Danga, the place where the mridanga was broken.

The hostile Muslim kazi issued an order forbidding sankirtan. By his order, those who violated it were to be converted to Islam and forced to surrender all their possessions to the authorities. Although most of the Nadia-vasis, the residents of Navadvipa, panicked on hearing this order, Srivas Pandit only laughed at the ruler's fanaticism.

It was in the house of Srivas that Lord Gauranga-sundar revealed His divine form to all His eternal associates. In essence, the house of Srivas Pandit was the birthplace of Gauranga's sankirtan movement. Daily lectures on the Bhagavatam, nightly kirtans, and many confidential Vraja-lilas of Lord Gaura Raya took place there.

Srivas Pandit and Sri Advaita Acharya, elders of the brahmana community, dedicated all their strength and energy to spreading the Lord's harinama-sankirtan movement. They offered their bodies, minds, homes, families, and everything they possessed to Lord Gaura. They knew no Deity other than Him. Srivas Pandit maintained his entire family not because they were his relatives, but because they were loving servants of Sri Chaitanya.

In the Pancha-tattva, Srivas Pandit represents the marginal energy of God, the living being, or tatastha-jiva. The devotees headed by Srivas are described as parts of Lord Chaitanya's body: His eyes, ears, hands, disc, and other weapons. All of them took part in the pastimes of Sri Gaurasundar. With their help, Lord Gauranga spread the sankirtan movement.

Originally, Srivas Pandit is Narada Muni, the intergalactic preacher and eternal associate of the Lord. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.short_description: Appearance day of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj, observed on Utthana Ekadashi.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj was a prominent disciple of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad and the founder-acharya of Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math. He appeared in Kanchanpara, East Bengal, on Utthana Ekadashi in 1904, in a respected brahmana family.

His childhood name was Heramba Kumar. After coming to the lotus feet of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur, he received the name Hayagriva Das Brahmachari and became known for strong dedication, purity, and preaching spirit.

Srila Prabhupad had great confidence in him and engaged him in responsible service. He later accepted tridanda-sannyas and became known as Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj. He preached widely, especially in Assam and Bengal, and established Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math in 1953.

He inspired many devotees through strict practice, compassionate preaching, and deep loyalty to the mission of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur. His disappearance is remembered on Gaura Pratipad.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Appearance of Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Appearance day of Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj, observed on Gaura Chaturthi.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj was a senior disciple of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad and the founder-acharya of Sri Gopinath Gaudiya Math. He appeared on Gaura Chaturthi as Pramod Bhushan Chakraborty in a pious Bengali brahmana family. From childhood he showed deep attachment to worship and devotional service, especially to Sri Madan Mohan.

In his youth he came to Sridham Mayapur and received the association and shelter of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur. Under that divine guidance he dedicated his life to bhajan, preaching, writing, deity worship, and service to the Gaudiya Math mission.

He was known for humility, scriptural depth, careful standards of worship, and affectionate guidance to devotees. Many Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas honored him as a guardian of Srila Prabhupad Saraswati Thakur's current.

After many decades of service he established Sri Gopinath Gaudiya Math and continued to inspire devotees through hari-katha, publication, personal example, and worship of Sri Sri Radha-Gopinath. His disappearance is observed on Gaura Chaturdashi.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Appearance of Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Appearance day of Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Goswami Maharaj, disciple of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj and the first sannyasi of Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj.
events.full_description:
Today is the appearance day of Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Goswami Maharaj.

Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Maharaj received harinam and diksha from Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj, and sannyas from Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj. He was the first person to whom Srila Govinda Maharaj gave sannyas. Before sannyas he was known as Prapanna Krishna Brahmachari, and earlier as Partha Sarathi Goswami.

His parents, Rasa Raj Goswami and Mrinalini Goswami, were Gaudiya Vaishnava brahmanas from Assam, whose family had migrated there from the Sylhet region of present-day Bangladesh during the period of Indian independence. His father had many disciples in Assam, and from this devotional family Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Maharaj developed a deep longing for the highest type of siksha, spiritual instruction. That searching mood brought him to the lotus feet of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj.

Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Maharaj earned a master's degree in Bengali literature at the University of North Bengal, where he studied texts including Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita and the poetry of Jayadeva, Chandidas, and other Vaishnava authors.

As a young disciple, he fully surrendered to the lotus feet of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj. Their meeting took place in 1982. He helped establish and then maintained for nearly thirty years two Kolkata branches of Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math, and later served in the development of the memorial to Srila Krishnadas Kaviraj Goswami in Vrindavan Dham. He also played an important role in temple construction in Ekachakra Dham, the appearance place of Sri Nityananda Prabhu, and in Hapaniya Dham, the appearance place of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj.

He supervised the printing and publication of many Bengali books by Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj and Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj, and served many aspects of book distribution in India, including the Math's long-standing presence at the famous Kolkata Book Fair.

Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Maharaj is known for leading many parikramas of Nabadwip Dham, Vrindavan Dham, and Ekachakra Dham, for his inspired kirtan leadership, his deep humility, and the affectionate care he offers to travelling devotees from around the world.

For many years he served as an important connecting point between Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math and many other Gaudiya Vaishnava missions and institutions. He was very dear to many godbrothers of his Guru Maharaj, including Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Maharaj and Srila Bhakti Kumud Santa Maharaj. He travelled and gave hari-katha throughout India and also in Russia.

Among his outstanding qualities are his desire to harmonise and unite different Vaishnava streams, his service in leading parikramas in Nabadwip, Vrindavan, and Ekachakra, his dedication to printing and distributing books, and his direct service to Srila Sridhar Maharaj, near whom he lived in the Math for two years.

Srila Sridhar Maharaj entrusted him with important seva: caring for Western devotees, meeting them at the airport, arranging their accommodation, and attending to their needs. For about thirty years he served as the temple president in Kolkata. He participated in the building of the Math temple in Ekachakra, from the purchase of the land through the temple's construction, and also in the building of the temple in Hapaniya Dham.

Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Maharaj took him with him during visits to Russia and Europe.

When Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Maharaj received a donation in Radha Vrindavan Chandra, he instructed that a remembrance hall, a memorial to Srila Krishnadas Kaviraj Goswami, be established in Vrindavan. In accordance with this instruction, Srila Bhakti Prapanna Tirtha Maharaj collected and prepared the Sanskrit verses before each chapter and arranged for them to be engraved in that memorial.

His preaching extended beyond India, including Israel, Russia, and Australia. During the coronavirus period he preached widely and regularly online for devotees around the world.

He also actively served the construction of the Math temple in Nabadwip, at Kuliagram.

On 24 February 2020, the Deities Sri Sri Guru Gauranga Radha Madan Mohan were installed at the ashram in Nabadwip, Kuliagram Aparadha Bhanjan Path.

On 26 August 2020, on Sri Radhastami, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was installed at the Math in Nabadwip, Kuliagram Aparadha Bhanjan Path.

On 22 August 2021, on Balaram Purnima, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was installed at the Math in Vrindavan, Radha-kund.

On 19 August 2024, the Deities of Radha-Krishna were installed at the ashram on Radha-kund: Sri Sri Guru Gauranga Radha Gopinath Sundar Jiu.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad
events.name: Appearance of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad
events.short_description: Commemoration of the appearance day of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, the guru of Srila Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, appeared in Sri Kshetra Dham, Jagannath Puri, on February 6, 1874, in the family of Srila Satchidananda Bhaktivinod Thakur. As a child he quickly mastered the Vedas, memorized the Bhagavad-gita, and delighted in studying his father's philosophical works. Because of his inexhaustible store of knowledge, he became known as "the living encyclopedia."

He spoke powerfully against caste consciousness and philosophical deviations within Gaudiya Vaishnavism. He sought to unite the four Vaishnava sampradayas by publishing the best-known philosophical works of their representatives. Srila Saraswati Thakur earned the title Nrisimha Guru, the lion-guru, because of his fearless and direct preaching of Vaishnava teaching. Mayavadis would cross to the other side of the street as soon as they saw the "lion-guru." An inspired preacher, he was also endowed with many wonderful divine qualities and filled with ecstatic love of God. He established sixty-four maths throughout India, as well as in Burma, England, and Germany.

Srila Saraswati Thakur excavated the birthplace of Lord Chaitanya at Yogapith in Sridham Mayapur, despite fierce opposition from the money-minded caste Goswamis of Navadvipa. At that place he built a magnificent Gaudiya Math temple.

His three publishing presses, known as the brihat-mridanga, in Madras, Calcutta, and Krishnanagar, printed books, magazines, and newspapers through which he spread the message of Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu.

When asked why he published the daily spiritual newspaper Nadia Prakash, Srila Saraswati Thakur replied, "If an insignificant town can afford to publish five daily newspapers, why can we not publish, every second, a newspaper about what is taking place in the eternal, unfading world of the transcendental activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead on His limitless spiritual planets in Goloka Vrindavan?"

In addition to his father's works, he published many books, including Bhagavad-gita, Srimad-Bhagavatam, Chaitanya-bhagavata, Chaitanya-mangala, Prema-bhakti-chandrika, and his favorite book, Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita. He predicted that people in the West would study Bengali specifically to relish the nectar left by Srila Krishna Das Kaviraj in Chaitanya-charitamrita.

To expand the reach of his preaching, he introduced many innovations. Throughout India he arranged free theistic exhibitions and dioramas depicting the pastimes of Sri Krishna and Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Using the latest technology, he even created moving figures. To commemorate Lord Chaitanya's visits to certain holy places, he installed marble replicas of the Lord's lotus feet. Breaking with established conventions and traditions, he allowed his sannyasi disciples to wear kurtas and coats made by tailors, travel in automobiles and motorboats, and sent some of them to Europe to spread Mahaprabhu's message.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati's revolutionary preaching ideas arose from the principle of yukta-vairagya established by the rasa-acharya Sri Rupa Goswami. As an eternally liberated soul, Srila Saraswati Thakur knew how to engage maya, the illusory energy, in the service of Lord Krishna.

Following in the footsteps of Srila Thakur Bhaktivinod, he preached the social system of varnasrama to bring harmony to society and fill its spiritual vacuum. Upholding the teachings of Sri Rupa Goswami and Sri Raghunath Das Goswami, he taught the science of devotional service and showed thousands of people how to attain pure love for Sri Sri Gandharvika-Giridhari, Radha-Krishna.

Alongside the phenomenal success of his preaching in India, where he organized sixty-four maths, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur constantly inspired his disciples to preach Krishna consciousness throughout the world. Srila Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada brought this dream to life. When Srila Prabhupada was asked to describe his spiritual master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, he simply said, "What can I say? He was a man from Vaikuntha."

In the eternal pastimes of Radha-Krishna in Goloka Vrindavan, Srila Saraswati Thakur serves as Nayana-mani Manjari. His pushpa-samadhis are situated at Radha Kunda and in the Radha-Damodar temple.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Appearance of Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Appearance day of Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj, observed on Rama Navami.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj was a disciple of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj and later served as acharya of Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math. He appeared on Sri Rama Navami in 1924 and from early life showed intelligence, discipline, and devotion.

He came under the shelter of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj and dedicated himself to guru-seva, study, preaching, and organizing the mission's service. He accepted sannyas and became widely known for deep scriptural command, powerful hari-katha, humility, and personal care for devotees.

Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Maharaj travelled and preached throughout India and abroad, wrote and published Vaishnava literature, and guided many seekers in the line of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur.

His appearance and disappearance are both connected with Navami tithi: his appearance is observed on Rama Navami and his disappearance on Krishna Navami.

events.subject: Sri Srimad Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Gosvami Maharaj
events.name: Appearance of Srila Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Gosvami Maharaj
events.short_description: Appearance tithi of Sri Srimad Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Gosvami Maharaj. In 2026 it is observed as his 100th Avirbhav Tithi Mahotsav.
events.full_description:
Sri Srimad Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Gosvami Maharaj, affectionately addressed by many devotees as Srila Maharaj, appeared on Sayana Ekadashi in Sita-Ramapura, Bankura district, West Bengal, in a Cakravarti brahmana family of the Bharadvaja gotra. His life became a shining example of steady service to Sri Hari, Sri Guru, and the Vaishnavas.

In his youth he began visiting Sri Syamananda Gaudiya Math, where he heard Srimad-Bhagavatam and received the association of devotees. There he met Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Gosvami Maharaj, one of the foremost disciples of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur, who later became his Gurudev. In 1955 he left home and joined the newly established Sri Caitanya Gaudiya Math in Kolkata, receiving harinama and diksha on Sayana Ekadashi and the name Sri Narottama dasa brahmachari.

Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Gosvami Maharaj saw his dedication and entrusted him with many important services: managing Vraja-mandala and Navadvipa-dhama parikramas, arranging pilgrimages, exhibitions, preaching programs, and helping oversee the development of Sri Caitanya Gaudiya Math branches. In 1969 he received sannyasa and the name Sri Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Maharaj.

After the disappearance of his Gurudev he served for many years as secretary of Sri Caitanya Gaudiya Math. He was especially honored for his deep knowledge of Gaudiya Math history, his careful service to the Sarasvata line, his translations and publications, and his strong emphasis on Vaishnava-seva and glorification of the devotees.

Later he accepted the responsibility of initiating acharya as a service to his guru-varga and founded Visuddha Caitanya-vani Pracara Kendra. He continued to nourish devotees through hari-katha, remembrance of the acharyas, and affectionate guidance. He entered the eternal service of Sri Sri Radha-Krishna on September 5, 2017, on Ananta Chaturdashi, the disappearance day of Srila Haridas Thakur.

events.subject: Srila Vakreshvar Pandit
events.name: Appearance of Srila Vakreshvar Pandit
events.short_description: Commemoration of the appearance day of Srila Vakreshvar Pandit. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
A beautiful singer and dancer, Vakreshvar Pandit always pleased Lord Chaitanya through his service: in the sankirtan parties of Navadvipa, which he joined from their very beginning, in theatrical performances at Srivas Angan, and at the annual Ratha Yatra festival in Jagannath Puri.

Once, in the house of Srivas Thakur, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sang without stopping for three days, and Vakreshvar Pandit danced the entire time in extraordinary ecstasy. Hearing this news, people gathered from everywhere to take part in the kirtan. As night fell, more and more devotees continued to arrive.

Learning of this, Devananda Pandit became restless and also ran toward the place from which the kirtan was coming. The powerful form of Vakreshvar Pandit and the sweetness of his voice filled Devananda Pandit with amazement. He stood motionless for several hours. The night still did not end, and the crowd grew, becoming louder and louder, because everyone longed to see Vakreshvar Pandit dance. At that time Devananda Pandit, holding a cane in his hand, restrained and calmed the crowd.

When Vakreshvar Pandit, overwhelmed with ecstasy, collapsed to the ground after a long dance of complete self-forgetfulness, Devananda Pandit carefully lifted him and placed him on his lap, wiping the dust from the holy body of Vakreshvar Pandit with his own scarf. Lord Chaitanya said, "Vakreshvar, unfortunately I have only one wing, and that is you; if I had a second wing, I could soar in the clouds."

Vrindavan Das Thakur wrote: "To awaken the sleeping souls of the age of Kali and distribute the nectar of Krishna's holy name, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu came. When He appeared, the mridangas and karatals sounded like thunder. Absorbed in the mood of ecstatic love and crying, 'Hari bol! Hari bol!' Sri Gauranga asked everyone without exception to chant the holy names of Krishna. Raising His golden arms to the sky, Lord Gaura Hari began to dance in ecstasy. At that very time Vakreshvar Pandit and the other devotees joined the Lord's dance." (Chaitanya-bhagavata)

Vakreshvar's blessing freed Devananda Pandit from the consequences of offending Srivas Pandit. Only after this did Sri Chaitanya accept Devananda Pandit among His devotees. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said of this incident, "Krishna has made His residence in the heart of Vakreshvar Pandit. And when Krishna begins to dance in his heart, Vakreshvar himself begins to dance. Any place blessed by Vakreshvar's presence becomes a place of pilgrimage far more sacred than all other holy places."

Some great devotees, such as Vakreshvar Pandit, Paramananda Puri, Svarupa Damodar, Gadadhar, Jagadananda Pandit, Shankara, Raghunath Vaidya, and Raghunath Das, associated with Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu from the very beginning of His manifest pastimes in Navadvipa. They also faithfully continued serving the Lord after He moved to Nilachala, Jagannath Puri.

Vakreshvar Pandit installed the Deities of Sri Sri Radha-Kantha in the house of Kashi Mishra. Kavi Karnapura states that Vakreshvar Pandit was an incarnation of Aniruddha of the Chatur-vyuha. Vakreshvar Pandit initiated Gopal Guru Goswami and many other devotees in Orissa. Dhyan Chandra, the disciple of Gopal Guru Goswami, wrote in his book that Vakreshvar Pandit is an incarnation of Tungavidya Sakhi, the expert singer and dancer who is one of Srimati Radharani's eight principal sakhis. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis.

events.subject: Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur
events.name: Appearance of Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur
events.short_description: Commemoration of the appearance day of Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur was born four years after Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa. His mother was Sri Narayani Devi, the niece of Srivas Pandit.

Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur describes how his mother received the mercy of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu when she was only four years old. He ordered Narayani to chant the Name of Krishna. She became maddened with love of God and began crying out, "O Krishna!" She was filled with divine love. Very often she received the remnants of Mahaprabhu's meal. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu loved her dearly. By His mercy, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur, the incarnation of Vyasa, the author of the Vedas and the Vedic scriptures, was born from her womb.

All his thoughts were filled with Sri Sri Gaura-Nityananda. Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur's father passed away before his birth. Left without a husband, Narayani soon became very poor, and eventually she settled in the house of Sri Vasudeva Datta Thakur in Mamagachi, where she helped with the household work. In that house Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur began his education.

Vrindavan often played in the house of Malini Devi, the wife of Srivas Thakur, and he grew up there. They cared for him as their dearest treasure. When Mahaprabhu left this world, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur was about twenty years old. Sri Nityananda Prabhu gave him initiation. He was the last disciple to whom Sri Nityananda Prabhu gave initiation.

Together with Nityananda Prabhu's wife, Jahnava Mata, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur went to the Kheturi Maha-mahotsava, the first great festival of Sri Gaura Purnima.

Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur wrote Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata. At first his book was called Sri Chaitanya-mangala. In it he describes the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates, with special detail given to the Lord's early lila.

In Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 20.82, Srila Krishna Das Kaviraj Goswami expresses his humility and gratitude to Vrindavan Das Thakur by calling him Vyasa: "Vrindavan Das Thakur is the beloved devotee of Lord Nityananda. Therefore he is the incarnation of Vyasadeva, who described the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Just as Srila Vyasadeva described the pastimes of Sri Krishna in the Bhagavatam and other Puranas, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur described Chaitanya-lila in Chaitanya-bhagavata."

The heart of humble Krishna Das Kaviraj rejoiced when he glorified Vrindavan Das Thakur: "Hearing Chaitanya-bhagavata destroys everything inauspicious. By reading Chaitanya-bhagavata, anyone can realize the greatness of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda and attain the highest perfection of knowledge: pure love for Krishna."

"It seems that Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Himself speaks to the reader through the mouth of Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur. I offer millions of respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Vrindavan Das Thakur. By writing this invaluable book, he delivered everyone without exception from the cycle of birth and death." (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 8.33-42)

In Mamagachi, Modadrumadvipa, Navadvipa, Vrindavan Das Thakur installed the Deities of Nitai-Gauranga and Sri Jagannath Deva. He lived there in a monastic way, worshiping his beloved Deities. Vrindavan Das Thakur had many disciples, including Gopinath Brahmachari, a descendant of Sri Keshava Bharati.

In Krishna-lila, Vrindavan Das Thakur is Sri Vyasadeva. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.full_description:
Vamshivadana Thakur is also known as Vamshi Das. Very little information about him has been preserved, but it is known that at the time of his birth Lord Chaitanya and Sri Advaita Prabhu were present in his home. Vamshivadana Thakur is known as the author of wonderful poems and songs that express the philosophy of Gaudiya Vaishnavism. He is considered an incarnation of the flute, vamshi, of Lord Muralimanohar. The writings of Vamshivadana Thakur carry an exceptionally sweet devotional mood.

After the disappearance of Srimati Vishnupriya Devi, Vamshi Das brought her Deity of Mahaprabhu to Koladvipa, present-day Navadvipa, and began worshiping Him there together with the Deity of Krishna named Pranavallabha.

Together with Nityananda Prabhu's wife, Jahnava Mata, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur went to the Kheturi Maha-mahotsava, the first great festival of Sri Gaura Purnima.

Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur wrote Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata. At first his book was called Sri Chaitanya-mangala. In it he describes the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates, with special detail given to the Lord's early lila.

In Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 20.82, Srila Krishna Das Kaviraj Goswami expresses his humility and gratitude to Vrindavan Das Thakur by calling him Vyasa: "Vrindavan Das Thakur is the beloved devotee of Lord Nityananda. Therefore he is the incarnation of Vyasadeva, who described the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Just as Srila Vyasadeva described the pastimes of Sri Krishna in the Bhagavatam and other Puranas, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur described Chaitanya-lila in Chaitanya-bhagavata."

The heart of humble Krishna Das Kaviraj rejoiced when he glorified Vrindavan Das Thakur: "Hearing Chaitanya-bhagavata destroys everything inauspicious. By reading Chaitanya-bhagavata, anyone can realize the greatness of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda and attain the highest perfection of knowledge: pure love for Krishna."

"It seems that Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Himself speaks to the reader through the mouth of Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur. I offer millions of respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Vrindavan Das Thakur. By writing this invaluable book, he delivered everyone without exception from the cycle of birth and death." (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 8.33-42)

In Mamagachi, Modadrumadvipa, Navadvipa, Vrindavan Das Thakur installed the Deities of Nitai-Gauranga and Sri Jagannath Deva. He lived there in a monastic way, worshiping his beloved Deities. Vrindavan Das Thakur had many disciples, including Gopinath Brahmachari, a descendant of Sri Keshava Bharati.

In Krishna-lila, Vrindavan Das Thakur is Sri Vyasadeva. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.full_description:
Srimati Krishnamayi Devi

Srimati Krishnamayi Devi was an eternal sevika of Nitya-lila-pravista Om Visnupad Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj and one of the great hidden supports of Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math. Her life stands as an example of complete dedication to Sri Guru, selfless service, and deep Vaishnavi bhakti.

In a pranam prayer composed by Sripad Bhakti Nanda Swami Maharaj, she is glorified as a siddha-sadhika, a giver of para-bhakti, filled with all forms of devotion, worthy of worship, and wholly dedicated to the lotus feet of Sri Guru and Krishna. The prayer says that through her selfless service to Sri Sri Guru-Gauranga, Radhika, and Krishna, she received the affectionate recognition of her Gurudev and naturally became an object of honor in the world of divine service.

She appeared in this world in December 1898, on Purnima, in an elevated smarta-brahmana family in Nagpur. Later her family settled in Tegharipara, a district of Navadvip. Her father was a lecturer at a local college, and from childhood she was familiar with the scriptures. Her husband held a responsible post as chief auditor of the Indian Railways. They had a daughter; later, after her husband's passing, she adopted a brahmana boy named Satya Hari.

After the division within the Gaudiya Math, Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj lived for more than a year in Navadvip at the house of Sripad Gopal Babu. He read Srimad-Bhagavatam, preached to the local people, and also spoke hari-katha in Mahaprabhu Mandir. At that time many in the Gaudiya Math did not know where he was staying, as Srila Guru Maharaj avoided crowds. Later Sripad Sakhu Baba found him and requested him not to remain hidden, since Srila Sridhar Maharaj was regarded as one of the finest preachers of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur.

After some time Srila Guru Maharaj agreed to establish a preaching mission. He built a small hut on land purchased by Sripad Sakhu Babu. Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math now stands on that land. In those days the area was still largely undeveloped.

Srimati Krishnamayi Devi used to go daily to the Ganga for bathing. When she heard about Srila Sridhar Maharaj, she changed her usual route so that she could regularly come and hear his hari-katha. She brought him flowers and Ganga water. This continued for about two and a half years, and at the age of thirty-seven she received Harinam initiation from him.

When her daughter had completed her education and her adopted son had become independent, Srimati Krishnamayi Devi decided to leave family life. She sold her property and offered everything to Srila Guru Maharaj. She told her family that there would be no inheritance, because the land and houses would be given to Srila Guru Maharaj's preaching mission. With those funds, rooms began to be built where devotees could reside. In this way her sacrifice became part of the early foundation and strengthening of Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math.

In the Math she served quietly but with great responsibility. She cared for the women devotees, prepared garlands for the Deities, maintained Srila Gurudev's room, and made sure that the water he liked to drink was always available. When Srila Guru Maharaj went out preaching, responsibility for the temple rested upon her, and many important decisions were made with her consent. Srila Guru Maharaj valued her selfless service, honesty, dedication, literary work, and poetry. He said that she was a special devotee and that the devotees should always care for all her needs.

In Tegharipara, where she lived, many people had formerly been absorbed in tantric practices. Srimati Krishnamayi Devi preached to them and brought many of them to Vaishnavism. Srila Guru Maharaj deeply appreciated this service and declared her to be a suddha-bhakta, a pure devotee of the Lord.

Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Maharaj was deeply impressed by her selfless dedication to Srila Sridhar Maharaj and connected her name with Srimati Radharani, who is also known as Krishnamayi. He explained this through the verse from Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita: “Krishnamayi means that within and without her there is only Krishna. Wherever her glance falls, Krishna manifests there.” In another sense, Krishna is composed of prema-rasa, and His Shakti is one with Him.

She was spoken of as Vaishnavi-shakti. Srila Yayavar Goswami Maharaj said that had she not been a woman, she would have been an acharya. Yet for those who do not see a Vaishnava through the external designations of male or female, she was already an acharya: through her example, her devotion, and her complete belonging to Srila Sridhar Maharaj. She did not need to display scholarship or outward preaching strength; her example was stronger than many lectures.

On the morning of the 25th day of Vamana in the year 516 of the Gaura era, July 19, 2002, on Gaura Dashami, in Sri Navadvip Dham, on Koladvip, non-different from Sri Govardhan, Srimati Krishnamayi Devi entered the eternal service of her Gurudev. She departed at 6:48 a.m. while the devotees were singing Mangala-arati, at the words “Jaya Sachinandana Sura-Muni-vandana”.

The day before her departure, she told her sevika Jahnava that her body should be given to fire. When Jahnava said that then the devotees would have no samadhi of hers, Krishnamayi Devi replied that the present devotees would serve it, but a future generation might destroy it and commit aparadha. Therefore, out of compassion for future generations, she asked that her body simply be offered to fire.

Her departure was quiet and unnoticed, without illness or outward signs. Thus Srimati Krishnamayi Devi, the eternal sevika of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj, completed the visible portion of her service and entered the unseen eternal service of Sri Guru, Sri Gauranga, and Sri Sri Radha-Krishna.
