events.subject: День ухода Шаранги Тхакура
events.name: Disappearance of Sharangi Tkhakura
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День ухода Шаранги Тхакура". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Srila Prabhupada, referring to the Anubhashya of Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, writes: "Another name of Thakur Saranga Das is Sharnga Thakur. Sometimes he is also called Sharngapani or Sharngadhara. He lived in Navadvipa, on Modadrumadvipa, and worshiped the Supreme Lord in a secluded place on the bank of the Ganga. He did not accept disciples, but the Supreme Lord from within his heart repeatedly urged him to do so. One morning he decided, 'The first person I see today will become my disciple.'

"When he went to the Ganga to bathe, he happened to notice a corpse floating in the river and touched it with his foot. The dead body immediately came back to life, and Thakur Saranga accepted him as his disciple. This disciple later became famous as Thakur Murari.

"His name is inseparably connected with the name of Sri Saranga. His spiritual descendants still inhabit the village of Shar. In Mamagachi there is a temple that is said to have been founded by Saranga Thakur. Not long ago a new temple was built there opposite the bakula tree, and it is now managed by members of the Gaudiya Math.

"The Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (172) states that Saranga Thakur was formerly the gopi named Nandimukhi. Some devotees say that he was Maharaj Prahlad, but Sri Kavi Karnapura, citing his father Shivananda Sen, does not accept that opinion." (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 10.113, purport)

The young man initiated by Saranga Thakur came from a fairly wealthy family, and his wedding was to take place that very day. But just before the joyful occasion, he was bitten by a cobra and died immediately. According to Bengali tradition, a person bitten by a snake is not cremated, so the body was wrapped in a harinama-chadar and placed in the river. Saranga Thakur whispered the mantra into his ear, and the young man returned to life. His name was Murari.

When Lord Chaitanya heard the news that Thakur had gained a disciple, He was very pleased and came to his house with a great crowd of devotees to see the extraordinary young man. The father and mother of Murari, overcome with grief, later heard that their son had not died and was now living in the village of Mamagachi. Coming there, they tried to persuade the young man to return home, but he told them, "You gave me only a dead body, while my spiritual master brought it back to life. Therefore I will remain with him."

The Chaitanya-bhagavata describes the extraordinary behavior of a saint named Murari Chaitanya Das. Some believe this refers to the young man revived by Saranga Thakur; others say it refers to Saranga Thakur himself, who is sometimes called Saranga Murari.

Opposite the temple of Saranga Murari grows a bakula tree more than five hundred years old. Lord Chaitanya loved to rest beneath it when returning from philosophical debates in Vidyanagar. Saranga Thakur often chanted his mantra beneath this tree. It gave shade and thus assisted his bhajan. Once, noticing that the tree had begun to dry up, Lord Chaitanya performed a miracle. He embraced it, and the tree came back to life. In this way He showed how dear to Him are those who serve His devotees. To this day, although its core is almost completely hollow, the tree continues to grow and bear flowers and fruit.

events.subject: День ухода Шридхары Пандита

events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День ухода Шридхары Пандита". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Kholavecha Sridhar, whose nickname means "banana seller," was a very poor brahmana. It is described that he was so poor he lived in a hut with an old, leaky roof. He had no money for proper utensils, so he drank water from an old cracked iron pot. When Kholavecha Sridhar chanted the Hare Krishna mantra at night, his neighbors thought he did so because hunger kept him from sleeping. Kholavecha Sridhar had a small plot of land with a banana grove. He earned his living by gathering leaves, bark, and pith from banana trees and selling them daily in the market. Despite his poverty, he spent half of his income on worshiping the Ganga and kept the other half for his own needs.

Kholavecha Sridhar was a great devotee of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who was very attached to him. In His youth, Chaitanya came to the market every day and bought pumpkins and bananas from Kholavecha Sridhar, as well as roots, stems, and flowers. Loving quarrels often took place between them because Chaitanya refused to pay the requested price. Angered, Sridhar would argue with Chaitanya and send Him to shop somewhere else. Then Chaitanya would simply take whatever He needed and leave without paying a coin. Sridhar would catch Chaitanya and bring Him back, lamenting, "I am only a poor old brahmana. And the little I receive I spend on worshiping the Ganga." In the end, Kholavecha Sridhar agreed to give Chaitanya a few bananas every day for free.

When Chaitanya began the civil-disobedience movement against the Muslim ruler of Navadvipa, Sridhar joined thousands of other Vaishnavas in the street kirtan, dancing with joy. It is also described that Chaitanya often drank water from his pot. Shortly before Chaitanya accepted sannyasa, Sridhar brought a pumpkin to Shachidevi so she could cook it for her son.

After Chaitanya settled in Puri, Kholavecha Sridhar came there every year to see Him. According to Kavi Karnapura, in Krishna's pastimes in Vrindavan Kholavecha Sridhar was a cowherd boy named Kusumasava. The Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (133) says, "The cowherd boy named Kusumasava, who took part in Krishna-lila, later became Kholavecha Sridhar in the lila of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu in Navadvipa."

A pushpa-samadhi of Kholavecha Sridhar is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

In his purports to the Bhagavata Purana, Srila Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada says of Kholavecha Sridhar: "Here is a typical example of how a poor man with no material possessions can become a most exalted devotee of the Lord. Thus material wealth will not help us attain shelter at the lotus feet of Lord Krishna or Sri Chaitanya Gosani; that shelter can be attained only through pure devotional service."

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj, observed on Gaura Pratipad.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj was a prominent disciple of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad and the founder-acharya of Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math. He appeared in Kanchanpara, East Bengal, on Utthana Ekadashi in 1904, in a respected brahmana family.

His childhood name was Heramba Kumar. After coming to the lotus feet of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur, he received the name Hayagriva Das Brahmachari and became known for strong dedication, purity, and preaching spirit.

Srila Prabhupad had great confidence in him and engaged him in responsible service. He later accepted tridanda-sannyas and became known as Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj. He preached widely, especially in Assam and Bengal, and established Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math in 1953.

He inspired many devotees through strict practice, compassionate preaching, and deep loyalty to the mission of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur. His disappearance is remembered on Gaura Pratipad.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj, observed on Gaura Chaturdashi.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Pramod Puri Dev Goswami Maharaj was a senior disciple of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Goswami Prabhupad and the founder-acharya of Sri Gopinath Gaudiya Math. He appeared on Gaura Chaturthi as Pramod Bhushan Chakraborty in a pious Bengali brahmana family. From childhood he showed deep attachment to worship and devotional service, especially to Sri Madan Mohan.

In his youth he came to Sridham Mayapur and received the association and shelter of Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur. Under that divine guidance he dedicated his life to bhajan, preaching, writing, deity worship, and service to the Gaudiya Math mission.

He was known for humility, scriptural depth, careful standards of worship, and affectionate guidance to devotees. Many Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas honored him as a guardian of Srila Prabhupad Saraswati Thakur's current.

After many decades of service he established Sri Gopinath Gaudiya Math and continued to inspire devotees through hari-katha, publication, personal example, and worship of Sri Sri Radha-Gopinath. His disappearance is observed on Gaura Chaturdashi.

events.subject: Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj, observed on Krishna Navami.
events.full_description:
Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Goswami Maharaj was a disciple of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj and later served as acharya of Sri Chaitanya Gaudiya Math. He appeared on Sri Rama Navami in 1924 and from early life showed intelligence, discipline, and devotion.

He came under the shelter of Srila Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj and dedicated himself to guru-seva, study, preaching, and organizing the mission's service. He accepted sannyas and became widely known for deep scriptural command, powerful hari-katha, humility, and personal care for devotees.

Srila Bhakti Vallabha Tirtha Maharaj travelled and preached throughout India and abroad, wrote and published Vaishnava literature, and guided many seekers in the line of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur.

His appearance and disappearance are both connected with Navami tithi: his appearance is observed on Rama Navami and his disappearance on Krishna Navami.

events.subject: Srila Govinda Ghosh Thakur
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Govinda Ghosh Thakur
events.short_description: Commemoration of the disappearance day of Srila Govinda Ghosh Thakur. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Govinda Ghosh and his brothers, Vasudeva Ghosh and Madhava Ghosh, were close associates of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda. Govinda Ghosh was also known as Ghosh Thakur. He was famous for his beautiful kirtans at the annual Ratha Yatra festival in Jagannath Puri. Lord Chaitanya would immediately begin to dance as soon as he started singing.

One day after lunch, Lord Chaitanya looked at a haritaki fruit, and Govinda, noticing this, rushed to the village to collect such fruits and offer them to the Lord. Receiving the haritaki so quickly, Lord Chaitanya told him, "Govinda, since you have not been able to give up the habit of keeping things in reserve, it is better for you to stay here and serve the Deity." Following this instruction, Govinda remained in Agradvipa, not far from Katwa. Yet despite the Lord's consoling words, he felt that Lord Chaitanya had left him behind.

A few days later, when Govinda dove deeply into the Ganga, something touched his back. It was a heavy piece of wood. That same night he received a divine instruction in a dream: he was to keep what he had found and give it to Lord Chaitanya when He came. Govinda understood that it was a Krishna-shila. The next morning Lord Chaitanya returned to Govinda's house and said, "Look here. You have nothing more to worry about. Tomorrow a sculptor will come here to make a Deity from this shila, and you will install Him."

Later, by the Lord's instruction, Govinda married and continued serving the Deity together with his wife. After some time Govinda was blessed with a son. Soon, however, both his wife and his son passed away. Govinda was so overwhelmed with grief that he even stopped serving Gopinath. Then Gopinath appeared to him in a dream and asked, "Govinda, do you think it is right that when a person loses one son, his other son should starve to death?" Govinda replied, "I had hoped that my son would live and perform all the necessary rites in remembrance of my departed soul. Tell me, what will I gain by serving You?" Krishna declared, "I promise that I will always observe the anniversary of your disappearance properly. Now, may I have something to eat?" Govinda was delighted and immediately resumed his service to Gopinath.

In time, Govinda Ghosh left his body. Then Gopinathaji Himself, holding kusha grass in His hands, began to perform the shraddha ceremony. From that time until today, every year on the disappearance day of Govinda Ghosh, his Deity performs the shraddha ceremony.

events.subject: Srila Haridas Thakur
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Haridas Thakur
events.short_description: Commemoration of the disappearance day of Srila Haridas Thakur. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Haridas Thakur is one of the closest associates of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Every day he chanted 300,000 holy names of the Lord. Mahaprabhu called him Namacharya, the spiritual teacher of chanting the Holy Name. Together with Nityananda Prabhu, by the order of Sri Chaitanya, he preached the glory of the Holy Name in Bengal. He spent the final years of his holy life in Puri, where he left his body in Mahaprabhu's arms while chanting the Hare Krishna maha-mantra. His life and preaching activities may be read about in Srila Krishnadas Kaviraj Goswami's Chaitanya-charitamrita and Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur's Chaitanya-bhagavata. The teachings of Haridas Thakur on the nature of Krishna's Holy Name, the greatness and goal of chanting it, and the offenses to be avoided in that chanting are presented in detail by Srila Bhaktivinod Thakur in his book Harinama-chintamani, in the form of conversations between Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Haridas Thakur.

He was born in a Muslim family living in the village of Budham near Vanagram in West Bengal. The spiritual inclinations formed in his previous lives manifested in him from a very early age; later he left home and family and turned completely to devotional service. In the forest of Benapasa he built himself a small hut and began intense chanting and meditation. Malicious people disturbed his bhajan, and therefore he left his hut and moved to a holy place on the bank of the Ganga. Even there, shameless people sent a young prostitute to him, hoping he would break his spiritual vows. But she was purified by the chanting of Srila Haridas Thakur; she became a devotee and gave up her former occupation. Srila Haridas Thakur initiated her into harinama and settled her in his hut in Benapasa, while he himself left that area.

Absorbed in chanting the Holy Name, he wandered along the banks of the Ganga until he reached the house of Srila Yadunandan Acharya in Santagram. He became a frequent guest of Hiranya and Govardhan Mazumdar, the landholders of Santagram. The latter was the father of Sri Raghunath Das Goswami. A low-class brahmana named Gopal Chakravarti spoke offensively and maliciously about Srila Haridas Thakur's explanation of the greatness of the Holy Name. Hiranya Mazumdar and his brother immediately removed Gopal Chakravarti from his position. Soon afterward he developed leprosy in his throat. This news shocked Srila Haridas Thakur. He left that place and came to Phulia, under the shelter of Advaita Acharya. He lived in a cave on the bank of the Ganga, absorbed in chanting and meditation.

A sincere devotee always avoids society and fame; he even feels aversion to them. Yet because of his purity he does not remain unknown. When Srila Haridas Thakur's name and reputation spread, the Muslims became disturbed and hostile toward him. They arranged for the local Muslim ruler to sentence Srila Haridas Thakur to public, cruel punishment. Srila Haridas, being a very compassionate saintly soul, did not condemn his tormentors. Instead, he blessed them and forgave their offenses, then returned to his cave. Soon after this incident, Lord Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appeared in Navadvipa-dham. Together with Advaita Acharya, Srila Haridas Thakur surrendered to the lotus feet of Lord Chaitanya. Srila Haridas Thakur became known as Namacharya, the teacher and preacher of the Holy Name. When Lord Chaitanya settled in Jagannath Puri, He arranged a permanent place for Srila Haridas to live and perform bhajan near the famous Siddha Bakula tree.

Glorious was Srila Haridas Thakur's departure from the material world. Lord Chaitanya personally performed the final Vaishnava rites for Srila Haridas Thakur, from bathing his body in the ocean to burying his transcendental body in the sand.

events.subject: Disappearance of Srila Lochana Dasa Thakur
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Lochana Dasa Thakur
events.short_description: Detailed Russian source text has been imported for Disappearance of Srila Lochana Dasa Thakur. English editorial translation is pending.
events.full_description:
Srila Lochan Das Thakur was born in the family of a brahmana who lived in Radha-desh, in Mahakumar near Katwa, in the district of Burdwan, Bengal. When he was only a small boy, he was fortunate to meet the devotees of Sri Gauranga. His guru was Narahari Sarkar Thakur. Srila Lochan Das's father was Sri Kamalakar Das, and his mother was Sri Sadanandi. Lochan Das was his father's only son, and his parents loved him dearly. He spent a good part of his life in the home of his grandparents. In the bloom of youth he went to Sri Khanda, where he met his Gurudev, Sri Narahari Sarkar Thakur. He lived there for some time and then received instruction in kirtan.

Lochan Das Thakur wrote Chaitanya-mangala, which describes pastimes of Lord Chaitanya not revealed in the works of Vrindavan Das Thakur and Krishna Das Kaviraj. In particular, he recounts the extraordinarily touching conversation between Sri Gaurasundar and Vishnupriya Devi on the evening before He accepted sannyasa. In earlier times, the poets of Bengal composed sacred songs and verses in various classical rhymes and meters called panchali. The panchali style was especially used to glorify the Lord. Srila Lochan Das Thakur used this form of poetry in writing his famous work, Sri Chaitanya-mangala. Panchali employs five different singing styles. Being a gifted musician, Lochan Das described Mahaprabhu's lilas in wonderfully poetic images filled with inspiration. Ordinary people could easily understand the divine qualities manifested in the character of Sri Chaitanya, and these qualities awakened their religious feeling. Just as devotees commonly recite the Vedic histories of the Ramayana and Mahabharata, wandering Gaudiya Vaishnavas in Bengal still recite stories from Chaitanya-mangala.

In addition, Lochan Das Thakur wrote many songs glorifying Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Sri Nityananda Prabhu, and Gauridas Pandit. Lochan Das emphasized that raganuga-bhakti should be practiced by taking shelter of Gadadhar Vrindavaneshvari, through which one may attain prema-bhakti for Radha-Govinda.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur printed and distributed Lochan Das Thakur's Chaitanya-mangala. Srila Prabhupada was very fond of his bhajans. Once he sang Parama Karuna, immersed in the ocean of gaura-prema. Prabhupada wrote an extensive commentary on this bhajan: "Lochan Das asks everyone he meets, 'My dear brother, simply worship Lord Chaitanya and Nityananda with firm faith and conviction. Do not think that this chanting and dancing will not bring you to the cherished goal. It certainly will. Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu assures us of this: one can attain perfection by this process. Therefore one should chant the holy name with firm determination and conviction.'"

His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.subject: Srila Narahari Sarkar Thakur
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Narahari Sarkar Thakur
events.short_description: Commemoration of the disappearance day of Srila Narahari Sarkar Thakur. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Before meeting Mahaprabhu, Narahari wrote many songs in Sanskrit and Bengali dedicated to the Vraja-rasa of Radha-Giridhari. Together with Gadadhar Pandit, he never left Lord Chaitanya. Narahari usually pleased the Lord by fanning Him with a chamara or a peacock-feather fan. In his song Gaura-arati, Srila Bhaktivinod Thakur wrote the words: narahari adi kori chamara dhulaya.

The family of Narahari Sarkar was the pride of the whole Vaishnava community. Through their association, all of Sri Khanda became an abode of Vaishnavas. The entire village became a branch of the desire tree of love of God. Thus, in the time of Lord Gaurachandra, Sri Khanda became a preaching center of Gaudiya Vaishnavism. Once Sri Nityananda Prabhu came to Sri Khanda. Meeting Narahari, He asked him, "So, We know who you are. Where is the honey?" By his mystic power, Narahari transformed the water in a vessel into honey and offered it to the Lord. In Vraja-lila, Narahari serves Lord Shyamasundar as Madhumati, a prana-sakhi who supplies Radha-Damodar and Their companions with sweet honey.

"Sri Narahari Sarkar was filled with prema for Radha-Krishna. No one can measure the depth of his devotion and pure love for Radha and Krishna. In Vraja he is Radharani's dear sakhi named Madhumati, the vessel of sweetness. In Gaura-lila he became Narahari, the vessel of prema for Radha-Krishna." (Sri Chaitanya-mangala)

Narahari Sarkar's books, Padakalpataru and Krishna-bhajanamrita, include intimate songs glorifying Lord Gauranga and Sri Nityananda Prabhu.

In Sri Krishna-bhajanamrita, Narahari gives instructions on worshiping Sri Krishna and Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

events.subject: Srila Narottam Das Thakur
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Narottam Das Thakur
events.short_description: Commemoration of the disappearance day of Srila Narottam Das Thakur. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Narottam Das Thakur was an embodiment of the Gaudiya teaching. He transmitted love of God through the poetry we know, and just as poetically he embodied that love in his own life. He was a perfect devotee, the ideal of a divine messenger, possessing the qualities described by the Six Goswamis whenever their pens touched palm leaves. The essence of Gaudiya Vaishnava philosophy is reflected in all his songs and ideals. Two important events preceded the appearance of Narottam Das Thakur: first, the appearance in this world of Lokanath Goswami, and second, the prediction of his birth by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

As stated in Narottam's writings, he outlived Jiva Goswami and his best friend Ramachandra Kaviraj. Just as he deeply felt separation from Mahaprabhu and from Radha and Krishna, he also acutely felt separation from his exalted contemporaries. Narottam's biographers always describe him in a state of divine bliss and sorrow, which, according to Vaishnava doctrine, awakens the highest spiritual feelings. Describing Narottam's condition, they write that "he constantly watered the earth with streams of tenderness flowing from his pious eyes." With unparalleled intensity he longed for God and His associates.

At last Narottam could no longer bear love in separation and joined the Lord in the spiritual world. In the house of Ganga Narayan Chakravarti in Murshidabad, he entered trance, completely absorbed in the lilas of Radha and Krishna. This continued for several days, convincing many that Narottam was about to leave this world. Yet at that solemn moment, some of his most zealous opponents, caste brahmanas, began mocking him. "Just look," they cried, "all his life he initiated brahmanas, though he was only a low-born shudra, and now he is dying as a shudra." Ganga Narayan Chakravarti could not bear these slanders and began praying to his guru: "Please return. Show them that they are simply fools." At that moment Narottam's body shone, and a golden brahmana thread mystically appeared on him. Seeing this miracle, the caste brahmanas immediately recognized their mistake and surrendered at Narottam's feet, begging forgiveness.

Narottam-vilasa tells a somewhat different story. Narottam asked his disciples to take him to Budhari and then to Gambhila so that he could bathe in the Ganga. Suddenly he was seized by a severe fever and understood that he might soon die. Without delay, he ordered his disciples to prepare a funeral pyre. Naturally, this was not easy for them, but they obeyed their guru's will. Narottam then sat silently for three days and left his body before many witnesses and disciples.

When his soul departed, the disciples seated his body on a decorated seat in the middle of the prepared pyre. It was then that the critical brahmanas began speaking maliciously in the presence of Ganga Narayan and other faithful followers of Narottam. Ganga Narayan could not tolerate it and prayed to Narottam to return and show mercy to these misguided brahmanas. At that moment Narottam's eyes opened, and he said, "Radha-Krishna-Chaitanya!" Moreover, his body shone like the sun, and the astonished brahmanas changed their view. All who witnessed this revival surrendered at Narottam's lotus feet. He embraced them all, bestowing precious bhakti upon them. He instructed them to study devotional literature under the guidance of Ganga Narayan Chakravarti, and then he left that place, wishing to meditate alone. During the last several months he displayed signs of ecstasy and constantly experienced separation from Sri Sri Radha and Krishna.

Narottam Das Thakur wrote many songs, including Gauranga Bolite Habe, Radha Krishna Prana Mora, and Je Anilo Prema Dhana.

events.subject: День ухода Шрилы Прабхупады
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Prabkhupady
events.short_description: Imported calendar reference for "День ухода Шрилы Прабхупады". English summary still needs editorial translation; the Russian source summary is linked in source_url.
events.full_description:
Dear Srila Prabhupada, please accept my most humble obeisances in the dust of your lotus feet.

Today is the anniversary of your departure from this world. You once said that when the Lord disappears from this world, at that same moment He appears somewhere in another universe to begin His pastimes again. You gave the analogy of the sun: when it disappears below the horizon and darkness descends, it simultaneously appears on the other side of the earth, giving the gentle rays of the morning dawn.

In the same way, your departure from our lives cast us into a long night of darkness that has never fully lifted. There is no doubt that your appearance somewhere else brought immense joy to those who welcomed you, but to this day the fire of separation from you still burns in my heart. According to accepted etiquette, such feelings are not often shared with others; rather, they are kept confidential and expressed only at appropriate moments, such as today.

Since the day you left, I have many times remembered the letter you wrote to me shortly after I joined your movement. It was as if even then you were preparing me with words of comfort for your inevitable departure from this world:

"I very much appreciate your feeling of separation after my departure from Detroit. I also feel separation from my Guru Maharaj, but I always feel that he is watching over me and protecting me."

Srila Prabhupada, I too would like to have such conviction, that you are always watching over me and protecting me, but I know that I must earn such mercy. The spiritual master is merciful by nature, but his association, like the association of the Lord, can be attained only through steady devotional service over many years, or even many lifetimes. Such association is not cheap, and it is never given casually.

In this life I had the opportunity to be in your association several times: in New York, when you gave me your dhoti, appreciating my service to your mission; on the flight to London, when we laughed heartily after you called Charlie Chaplin's playful antics Krishna's humor; and in your room at the temple on Bury Place, when you paternally patted me on the back. All of this was undoubtedly only your causeless mercy upon me.

Srila Prabhupada, I also long for your association and service to you. Therefore, on this auspicious day, I will draw my own conclusion from what the Lord spoke to Narada: I will refocus on the goal, and in the few years remaining in this life I will make every effort to attain perfection in service to you and to become free from all material desires.

Please help me throw out from my heart all unwanted things, so that I may become a valuable instrument in the service so dear to you: preaching the glories of your beloved Lord. Only by serving this mood of yours in the material world will I become eligible to serve your mood in the spiritual abode.

Many times I saw how strongly you wanted the conditioned souls of this world to hear the holy names of the Lord, read His words of wisdom, and enjoy food blessed by Him. Once I entered your room in New Mayapur and saw you looking out the window, watching hundreds of devotees begin to take prasadam. Turning, you looked at me and said nothing, but the tears rolling from your eyes were worth a thousand words. Your heart melted with compassion when you saw your devotees enjoying the Lord's mercy.

Srila Prabhupada, please raise me to the level where I too can weep out of compassion for the fallen souls and humbly go out every day to preach the divine instructions. In such a state of mind I will lose interest in all the temptations of this world, and my only desire will be to become your servant, life after life. Only through such service will I be able to attain your approval and one day realize the truth of the words you spoke to me: that you are in fact always watching over me and protecting me.

Your servant forever, Indradyumna Swami.

events.subject: Srila Ramachandra Kaviraj
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Ramachandra Kaviraj
events.short_description: Commemoration of the disappearance day of Srila Ramachandra Kaviraj. This event is matched by the Vaishnava tithi rule stored in the calendar database.
events.full_description:
Ramachandra Kaviraj was a disciple of Srila Srinivas Acharya and a close friend of Srila Narottam Das Thakur. Previously he was known as Tajniv Sen. He was born in Kumaranagar, and after marriage he moved to Sri Khanda.

"Tajniv Sen was a pure devotee, dearly loved by Narahari Sarkar and the other residents of Sri Khanda. He was extremely learned in all subjects, and his wife was very chaste and humble. Her activities were completely transcendental." (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.92)

"Ramachandra Kaviraj was a very sincere, beautiful, intelligent, energetic, and inspired devotee." This is how one of his biographers describes him. His maternal grandfather, Sri Damodar Kaviraj, was a famous poet. After the death of their father, the two brothers, Ramachandra and Govinda, moved to live with their grandfather. At that time Ramachandra practiced medicine and was already well known as a mature poet. He met Srinivas Acharya and Narottam Thakur on the way to his own wedding. This is how it happened.

A large wedding procession was moving along, and the groom was being carried in a palanquin. When the procession stopped under a tree near the ashram of Srinivas Acharya, Srinivas and Narottam were sitting together and speaking with one another. Srinivas Acharya said, "Look at this great wedding procession. They have spent so much effort just to become more deeply entangled in maya. They have placed the noose of maya around their own necks. This is a special way of tying a rope. When a person hangs himself, the noose tightens more and more until he suffocates. Yet people arrange such a great celebration to tighten this noose, and they do not understand it. Just look at this foolish spectacle. They perform these ceremonies without understanding what is truly auspicious and what is not." Hearing these words, Ramachandra Kaviraj did not continue to the wedding celebration. Instead, he returned home and then went to Srinivas Acharya, from whom he received initiation.

Although he was married, he and his wife Ratanala had no material attachments. They were fully absorbed in loving service to Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and had no children.

In Vrindavan, Sri Jiva Goswami gave him the title Kaviraj, "king among poets." Ramachandra wrote the books Smarana-darpana, Smarana-chamatkara, and Siddhanta-chandrika. He preached widely and initiated many disciples.

In Vraja-lila his name is Karuna Manjari. His principal disciple was Hariram Acharya. His samadhi is located in Dhira Samira Kunja beside the samadhi of Srinivas Acharya.

Narottam Das Thakur and Ramachandra lived together as best friends. Narottam Thakur was deeply attached to Ramachandra Kaviraj, and Ramachandra loved to speak with him on confidential subjects. Although Narottam was the godbrother of Srinivas Acharya and therefore stood on the same level as Ramachandra Kaviraj's guru, Narottam's closest associate was nevertheless the disciple of Srinivas Acharya.

Having received news of the disappearance of Ramachandra Kaviraj and, somewhat later, of Srinivas Acharya, Srila Narottam Thakur plunged into an ocean of separation and wrote songs that melt even a stone-like heart when heard:

prakashila mahaprabhu hare krishna mantra
premera vadara kari barila samsara
andha avadhi yata kare parsha
bindhu na padila mukhe ramachandra dasa

"Sriman Mahaprabhu is so kind that by His mercy He manifested the nectar of the Hare Krishna mantra. The Holy Name will deliver all souls from the cycle of birth and death, from the lower planets and hell. The Holy Name grants the taste of divine love for Radha-Madhava. Even the blind and the deaf, everyone, can drown in the ocean of prema. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu filled everyone with love of God. But Ramachandra Das is so unfortunate that he could not taste even a drop of this nectar."

events.subject: Srila Shivananda Sen
events.name: Disappearance of Srila Shivananda Sen
events.short_description: Srila Shivananda Sen cared for the devotees travelling every year to Jagannath Puri for Ratha Yatra.
events.full_description:
Every year, about a month before Chaturmasya, Srila Shivananda Sen led a group of roughly two hundred devotees to the Ratha Yatra festival in Jagannath Puri. He arranged their food, tolls, travel, and lodging, personally ensuring that the devotees had whatever they needed.

Shivananda Sen showed the compassion of a Vaishnava toward all living beings, whether human beings or animals. Once a stray dog joined the travelling party. Shivananda fed the dog and even paid for it to cross the river with the devotees. When the dog later disappeared, he sent many people to search for it. Upon reaching Puri, the devotees saw Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu throwing coconut pulp to that very dog. After tasting Mahaprabhu's maha-prasada, the dog became purified, and when it was no longer seen the next day, Shivananda Sen understood that by the Lord's mercy it had attained liberation.

While observing Chaturmasya in Puri, Shivananda and the other devotees regularly bathed in the blissful company of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. He used everything he possessed in the service of Krishna and the Vaishnavas. His whole family and servants were faithful followers of Lord Gauranga.

Kavi Karnapura, the son of Shivananda Sen, writes in Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika that Shivananda Sen was an embodiment of Sri Chaitanya Deva's love, and in Krishna-lila he is Vira-gopi, a messenger of Srimati Radharani. Devakinandan Das glorifies him: "I bow to Shivananda Sen, who is filled with divine love. For him, social position, life, and wealth are all embodied in the lotus feet of Sri Gaura Raya." His samadhi is situated among the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.subject: Sripad Ajita Krishna Brahmachari
events.name: Disappearance of Sripad Ajita Krishna Brahmachari
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Sripad Ajita Krishna Brahmachari, the devoted servitor remembered as Seva Saurabh Prabhu.
events.full_description:
The glories of Sripad Ajita Krishna Brahmachari.

By Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj

The following is an English translation of the article written in honour of the passing of Sripad Ajita Krsna Prabhu Seva Saurabh. It was first published in Sri Gaudiya Darsan in Volume 14, Issue 4, on Sunday, 19 September 1971.

Sripad Ajita Krishna Prabhu reaches the dust of the Holy Dham
Last Wednesday, 30 June 1971, the Math’s distinguished servitor—the best of Sri Guru-pada-padma’s single-minded servitors—the ever-smiling Sripad Ajita Krishna Brahmachari Seva Saurabh Prabhu suddenly left for his abode and immersed us all in an ocean of separation. Today it is painful to even think that this courageous, enthusiastic, resolute, tolerant, and single-minded servant of Sri Guru, Sripad Seva Saurabh Prabhu, who was a tireless worker and determined to make the impossible possible, is no longer externally present amongst us. His extraordinary qualities and extremely sweet behaviour equally attracted everyone, even if they were unacquainted with him, be they residents of the Math, householders, sannyasis, or townspeople. Thus, everyone is heartbroken and overwhelmed by separation from him.

His endeavours to serve were so extraordinary and broad that all the servants of the Math would get inspiration to perform their own services with more enthusiasm and natural satisfaction when they saw him covering and completing all of his services. Everywhere—whether on parikrama in Sri Nabadwip Dham, in Vrndavan, in Dvaraka, in Haridvar, in Ayodhya, in any other place in North India, in South India, or in Sri Kedar Badarik Asram—his service and companionship were completely indispensable. There was no place for even a moment of rest on the garland of his service and duties. Over the course of all his prolonged and extremely laborious service, no one would ever see him lay down to rest on a bed during a break time. Such was his enthusiasm for service. He was the ideal servitor: he engaged in service twenty-four hours a day, every day.

Almost twenty years ago today Sripad Ajita Krishna Prabhu joined Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math Nabadwip.

Prior to that, he frequented many Maths enquiring about spiritual life. Not finding satisfaction anywhere, he at last came at the request his Vartma-pradasak-guru Sriyukta Satyacharan Ghatak Mahasay—a long-time servitor of Sri Gaudiya Math—to the holy lotus feet of our Math’s Acharya, the supremely worshippable Parivrajakacharya-varya Om Visnupad Sri Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj, accepted Sri Hari-nam and gayatri-diksa from him, and dedicated his heart to the service of Sri Guru with great satisfaction.

His name in his previous asram was Sri Adhirachandra Majumadar. His only tie [at that time] was his mother. (She also later accepted initiation from Sri Guru Pada-padma.) Although he externally conducted himself like a householder as long as his mother lived, because there was no one to look after her, he never slackened his service to Sri Guru and Sri Gauranga. Even during his life as an employee of Bengal Immunity Co. Ltd., everyone knew of his exalted reputation and good name. Not only was he elected a ‘selected member’ of the said company’s ‘watch committee’ on account of his honesty and efficiency, but after his mother’s death, even after he resigned from his employment, offered all his wealth at the feet of Sri Guru, and embraced a life of constant service to the Lord in the Math, many of his friends and relatives who were enamoured by his qualities frequented the Math desiring to met with him and eventually took shelter of the Math as a result of his association. Furthermore, the said company also behaved extremely respectfully towards him [even after he resigned].

Although his detached household life was one of abundant affluence and furnishings, his service life in the Math was filled with service-based austerity, renunciation, unostentatiousness, and deep attachment to Sri Guru and Sri Gauranga. Although his destiny was to leave in Kedar Badarik Asram this year, he reversed this on the strength of his service, returned from there, and performed his Pastime of departing in Sri Gaura Dham, which he always cherished; souls with deep vision are praising his disappearance Pastime in this way.

When we think of his grand departure from the midst of Sri Guru and Sri Gauranga, Sri Gaura Dham, and Sri Ganga, and above all, his leaving one service to immediately engage himself in another, as the limit of his fortune cannot be ascertained, so we are not able to estimate our misfortune in being deprived of the great association of this exalted soul. “Svatantra Krishnera ichchha ha-ila sanga bhanga: Krishna’s independent will has broken that association” (Cc: Antya, 11.92). Although Sripad Seva Saurabh Prabhu is not personally in our midst today, we make only the small prayer at the feet of Sri Guru and Sri Gauranga that the Lord does not deprive us of his association eternally.

Reference
Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj also wrote the following Sanskrit poem as a tribute to Sripad Ajita Krsna Das Brahmachari Seva Saurabh which was published as a dedication at the beginning of the first Bengali edition of Sri Sri Prema-dhama-deva-stotram.

Utsarga Patram

An Explanatory Note

srimad ajita-krsnakhyo brahmachari cha dasakah
purvam srimad adhirakhyo majumadara itiritah [1]
utsargi-krta-sarvasvo guru-krsna-padambuje
mano-dhana-tanu-sraddha-guru-seva-sada-vratah [2]

Srimad Ajita Krishna Das Brahmachari, who was formerly known as Srimad Adhirachandra Majumadar, gave everything to the lotus feet of Sri Guru and Krishna, and constantly engaged in faithful service to Sri Guru with his body, mind, and wealth.

rasadri-veda-gaurabde suklasadhastami-tithau
prapto dhama-rajo-’chintyam sevartih sevakottamah [3]

On Gaura Astami in the month of Asadh in the year 485 of the Gaura era (Wednesday, 30 June 1971), he who was the best of all servitors and always anxious for service reached the inconceivable dust of the Holy Dham.

puta-seva-smrtes tasya sri-seva-saurabha-prabho
samraksane krtotsahair visva-srestha-hitaya cha [4]
gaura-gatha-maya-granthah prema-dhamas tavakhyakah
prakasito ’tra chaitanya-sarasvata-mathasritaih [5]

With great enthusiasm for preserving remembrance of Sri Seva Saurabh Prabhu’s pure service, and for the greatest benefit of the world, this book which is made up of the glories of Sri Gaura, Sri Sri Prema-dhama-deva-stotram, has been published here by the surrender souls of Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math.

events.name: Disappearance of Srivasa Pandit
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Srivasa Pandit, the dear associate of Sri Gauranga and one of the principal participants in Mahaprabhu's sankirtan pastimes.
events.full_description:
Srivasa Pandit is one of the eternal associates of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and is honored as the representative of pure devotional service among the Pancha-tattva. His home in Navadvipa, Srivasa Angan, became the sacred place of Mahaprabhu's nightly kirtans and many confidential sankirtan pastimes.

Srivasa Pandit lived with his brothers Sri Rama, Sri Nidhi and Sripati, worshiping Krishna and bathing daily in the Ganga. His wife, Malini Devi, was closely connected with Mother Sachi and cared for young Nimai with deep affection. In Gaura-lila, Srivasa Pandit offered his home, family, heart and life completely to the service of Sri Gauranga.

The disappearance day of Srivasa Pandit is observed on Ashadha Krishna Dashami, the tenth tithi of the waning half of the Ashadha month.

events.name: Disappearance of Tridandi-swami Srimad Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan Maharaj
events.short_description: Disappearance day of Tridandi-swami Srimad Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan Maharaj, observed on Vamana Gaura Dashami.
events.full_description:
Disappearance of Tridandi-swami Srimad Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan Maharaj

Srimad Madhusudan Maharaj received the title Bhakti Kamal, “the lotus of devotion”, from Srila Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakur while he was a brahmachari. When Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj gave him sannyas, he named him Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan.

Madhusudan is commonly understood as a name of the Lord connected with His killing of the demon Madhu. Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj, however, explained that madhu in the name Madhusudan may also mean “nectar”, “honey”, or, in a deeper sense, rasa. Thus Madhusudan may be understood as “one who relishes and absorbs rasa”. This meaning is sweetly expressed in the name Bhakti Kamal Madhusudan: “one who enjoys the nectar of the lotus of devotion”.

For a very long time Srimad Madhusudan Maharaj was a friend and affectionate well-wisher of Srila Bhakti Raksak Sridhar Dev-Goswami Maharaj and Srila Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswami Maharaj.

events.full_description:
Sri Vasudeva Ghosh, a close associate of Lord Chaitanya, was famous for his kirtans. The Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita says that when Vasudeva Ghosh led kirtan, even trees and stones melted upon hearing him. He composed many songs about Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Vasudeva Ghosh and his brothers Govinda and Madhava are eternal associates of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda. See Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi-lila 10.115, 11.14-15, 11.19, and 11.88.

Vasudeva Ghosh, together with his two brothers Madhava and Govinda, were eternal companions of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Sri Nityananda Prabhu. Established in madhurya-rasa, they accepted Sri Radhika as their supreme shelter, the ashraya-vigraha. All three brothers sang beautiful, sweet kirtans. Whenever they sang, Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda would enter ecstasy and begin to dance.

Every year they came to Jagannath Puri to take part in the Ratha Yatra festival. They led kirtan in one of the seven parties arranged by Lord Chaitanya. Vasudeva Ghosh used his music and singing to preach throughout Bengal. He wrote many Bengali songs about Lord Gauranga that devotees still sing today. In one of them he says, "If Lord Gaura had not appeared in this age of Kali, how would we have lived? He gave us the very essence, the very magic of life: divine love, without which it is impossible to live in this world. Without Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, how would we have known that Srimati Radharani holds the highest position in the world of divine love? Having received all this from the hands of Lord Gaurahari, we are certain that this life is worth living."

In another bhajan Vasudeva Ghosh says, "In Your former lilas, when You appeared as Lord Ramachandra, You became famous for building a bridge across the ocean to Sri Lanka. Now, in this Kali-yuga, You have built the bridge of harinama-sankirtan, by which even the lame and the blind can cross the ocean of birth and death and attain the highest spiritual happiness."

In the eternal nikunja-lilas of Radha-Madhava, he is Gunatunga Sakhi. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.

events.full_description:
Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur was born four years after Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa. His mother was Sri Narayani Devi, the niece of Srivas Pandit.

Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur describes how his mother received the mercy of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu when she was only four years old. He ordered Narayani to chant the Name of Krishna. She became maddened with love of God and began crying out, "O Krishna!" She was filled with divine love. Very often she received the remnants of Mahaprabhu's meal. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu loved her dearly. By His mercy, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur, the incarnation of Vyasa, the author of the Vedas and the Vedic scriptures, was born from her womb.

All his thoughts were filled with Sri Sri Gaura-Nityananda. Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur's father passed away before his birth. Left without a husband, Narayani soon became very poor, and eventually she settled in the house of Sri Vasudeva Datta Thakur in Mamagachi, where she helped with the household work. In that house Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur began his education.

Vrindavan often played in the house of Malini Devi, the wife of Srivas Thakur, and he grew up there. They cared for him as their dearest treasure. When Mahaprabhu left this world, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur was about twenty years old. Sri Nityananda Prabhu gave him initiation. He was the last disciple to whom Sri Nityananda Prabhu gave initiation.

Together with Nityananda Prabhu's wife, Jahnava Mata, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur went to the Kheturi Maha-mahotsava, the first great festival of Sri Gaura Purnima.

Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur wrote Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata. At first his book was called Sri Chaitanya-mangala. In it he describes the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates, with special detail given to the Lord's early lila.

In Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 20.82, Srila Krishna Das Kaviraj Goswami expresses his humility and gratitude to Vrindavan Das Thakur by calling him Vyasa: "Vrindavan Das Thakur is the beloved devotee of Lord Nityananda. Therefore he is the incarnation of Vyasadeva, who described the pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Just as Srila Vyasadeva described the pastimes of Sri Krishna in the Bhagavatam and other Puranas, Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur described Chaitanya-lila in Chaitanya-bhagavata."

The heart of humble Krishna Das Kaviraj rejoiced when he glorified Vrindavan Das Thakur: "Hearing Chaitanya-bhagavata destroys everything inauspicious. By reading Chaitanya-bhagavata, anyone can realize the greatness of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda and attain the highest perfection of knowledge: pure love for Krishna."

"It seems that Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Himself speaks to the reader through the mouth of Srila Vrindavan Das Thakur. I offer millions of respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Vrindavan Das Thakur. By writing this invaluable book, he delivered everyone without exception from the cycle of birth and death." (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 8.33-42)

In Mamagachi, Modadrumadvipa, Navadvipa, Vrindavan Das Thakur installed the Deities of Nitai-Gauranga and Sri Jagannath Deva. He lived there in a monastic way, worshiping his beloved Deities. Vrindavan Das Thakur had many disciples, including Gopinath Brahmachari, a descendant of Sri Keshava Bharati.

In Krishna-lila, Vrindavan Das Thakur is Sri Vyasadeva. His samadhi is located in the area of the sixty-four samadhis in Vrindavan.
